A00.d: Acute intestinal infection by toxigenic Vibrio cholerae, whose toxin causes massive secretion of water and electrolytes into the small intestine.

A01.d: Systemic infection by Salmonella Typhi or Paratyphi, acquired through contaminated water or food, with bacteremia and invasion of the reticuloendothelial system.
s: Abdominal pain and constipation or diarrhea

A02.d: Infections by nontyphoidal salmonellae, usually gastroenteritis after contaminated food, which may cause bacteremia and extraintestinal foci.

A03.d: Infection of the colon by Shigella, transmitted by the fecal-oral route with a low inoculum, which invades the mucosa and causes inflammatory colitis.

A04.d: Enteritis caused by bacteria such as pathogenic Escherichia coli, Campylobacter, Yersinia and Clostridioides difficile, with watery or inflammatory diarrhea.

A05.n: Other bacterial foodborne intoxications, not elsewhere classified
A05.d: Condition caused by ingestion of bacterial toxins preformed in food, such as those of Staphylococcus aureus, Clostridium and Bacillus cereus, or by botulism.
s: Outbreak among people who shared a meal

A06.d: Infection by the protozoan Entamoeba histolytica, which invades the colonic mucosa and may spread to the liver, forming abscesses.
s: Fever and right upper quadrant pain in liver abscess

A07.d: Intestinal parasitic infections by protozoa such as Giardia, Cryptosporidium, Balantidium and Cyclospora, transmitted by contaminated water and food.
s: Severe chronic diarrhea in immunosuppressed patients

A08.n: Viral and other specified intestinal infections
A08.d: Gastroenteritis caused by viruses such as rotavirus, norovirus and enteric adenoviruses, usually self-limited and transmitted by the fecal-oral route.
s: Dehydration in infants and the elderly

A09.n: Diarrhoea and gastroenteritis of presumed infectious origin
A09.d: Acute diarrhea of presumed infectious origin in which the agent is not identified, used when the clinical picture suggests an infectious etiology.

A15.n: Respiratory tuberculosis, bacteriologically and histologically confirmed
A15.d: Infection of the lungs or respiratory tract by Mycobacterium tuberculosis confirmed by sputum smear microscopy, culture, molecular testing or histology.
s: Cough for more than three weeks

A16.n: Respiratory tuberculosis, not confirmed bacteriologically or histologically
A16.d: Respiratory tuberculosis diagnosed by clinical, radiological and epidemiological criteria, without bacteriological or histological confirmation.
s: Infiltrate or cavitation on chest X-ray

A17.d: Involvement of the nervous system by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, mainly basal meningitis, tuberculomas and arachnoiditis.
s: Headache and fever with subacute course
CSF with lymphocytosis, high protein and low glucose

A18.d: Extrapulmonary tuberculosis in organs such as lymph nodes, bones, kidneys, intestine, pericardium and genital tract, through hematogenous or lymphatic spread.
s: Low back pain and vertebral deformity in Pott disease

A19.d: Massive hematogenous dissemination of Mycobacterium tuberculosis with multiple small foci in the lungs and other organs, common in immunosuppressed patients.
s: Diffuse micronodular infiltrate on chest X-ray

A20.d: Zoonosis caused by Yersinia pestis transmitted by rodent fleas or droplets, with bubonic, septicemic and pneumonic forms.
s: Pneumonia with hemoptysis in the pneumonic form

A21.d: Zoonosis caused by Francisella tularensis acquired through contact with animals, arthropod bites or inhalation, with ulceroglandular, pneumonic and typhoidal forms.

A22.d: Infection by Bacillus anthracis through contact with animals or animal products, or ingestion or inhalation of spores, with cutaneous, pulmonary and gastrointestinal forms.
s: Papule that progresses to a painless black eschar
Mediastinal widening in the inhalational form
Shock and hemorrhagic meningitis in severe forms

A23.d: Zoonosis caused by Brucella acquired through contact with animals or consumption of unpasteurized milk and dairy products, with an acute or chronic course.
s: Profuse sweating with a characteristic odor

A24.d: Infections by Burkholderia mallei (glanders) and Burkholderia pseudomallei (melioidosis), acquired from animals or from contaminated soil and water.
s: Multiple abscesses in skin and organs

A25.d: Infections by Streptobacillus moniliformis or Spirillum minus transmitted by the bite or scratch of rodents.

A26.d: Infection by Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae acquired by handling fish, meat or animals, usually cutaneous and localized to the hands.

A27.d: Zoonosis caused by Leptospira acquired through contact with water or mud contaminated by rodent urine, with diffuse vasculitis.
s: Orange-tinged (rubinic) jaundice and renal failure in the severe form

A28.n: Other zoonotic bacterial diseases, not elsewhere classified
A28.d: Bacterial zoonoses not listed in other categories, such as pasteurellosis after an animal bite and cat-scratch disease.
s: Cellulitis after a bite or scratch

A30.d: Chronic infection by Mycobacterium leprae with tropism for skin and peripheral nerves, whose clinical spectrum depends on the immune response.
s: Hypopigmented or reddish patch with altered sensation
Loss of thermal, pain and tactile sensation
Diffuse infiltration and nodules in multibacillary forms

A31.d: Infections by nontuberculous mycobacteria, such as Mycobacterium avium complex, M. kansasii and rapidly growing mycobacteria.
s: Chronic cough in patients with lung disease

A32.d: Infection by Listeria monocytogenes, acquired through contaminated food, severe in pregnant women, newborns, the elderly and immunosuppressed patients.

A33.d: Tetanus of the newborn due to contamination of the umbilical stump with Clostridium tetani spores, whose toxin blocks motor inhibition.
s: Difficulty sucking from the first days of life

A34.d: Tetanus acquired during pregnancy, abortion or the puerperium, due to contamination of the genital tract with Clostridium tetani spores.
s: History of delivery or abortion under inadequate conditions

A35.d: Accidental tetanus due to tetanus toxin produced in contaminated wounds, which blocks the release of inhibitory neurotransmitters.
s: Rigidity of axial and abdominal muscles

A36.d: Infection by toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae, with a pseudomembrane in the upper airways and systemic effects of the toxin.
s: Adherent grayish pseudomembrane in the oropharynx

A37.d: Highly contagious respiratory infection by Bordetella pertussis, with prolonged paroxysmal cough, severe in infants.

A38.d: Infection by group A beta-hemolytic streptococcus producing erythrogenic toxin, usually associated with pharyngotonsillitis.
s: Desquamation of hands and feet during convalescence

A39.d: Infection by Neisseria meningitidis, with meningitis and/or meningococcemia of rapid progression and high lethality.

A40.d: Sepsis caused by streptococci, such as Streptococcus pyogenes, agalactiae or pneumoniae, with a systemic inflammatory response and organ dysfunction.

A41.d: Sepsis due to other agents, such as Staphylococcus aureus, gram-negative bacilli and anaerobes, or due to an unspecified agent.

A42.d: Chronic suppurative infection by Actinomyces, bacteria of the oral flora, which forms abscesses with fistulas and crosses tissue planes.

A43.d: Infection by Nocardia acquired by inhalation or inoculation, with a predilection for the lungs, skin and central nervous system in immunosuppressed patients.
s: Subacute pneumonia with nodules or cavitation

A44.d: Infection by Bartonella bacilliformis transmitted by sand flies, with a febrile hemolytic phase and an eruptive phase with angiomatous lesions.

A46.d: Infection of the superficial dermis and lymphatics, usually by Streptococcus pyogenes, from a portal of entry in the skin.
s: Shiny erythematous plaque with well-demarcated borders
Location on the lower limbs or face

A48.n: Other bacterial diseases, not elsewhere classified
A48.d: Specific bacterial diseases not listed in other categories, such as gas gangrene, legionellosis, toxic shock syndrome and Brazilian purpuric fever.
s: Shock and organ dysfunction in toxemic forms

A49.d: Records a bacterial infection whose site is not specified, usually with an identified agent and no defined focus; the clinical picture depends on the agent and the site.

A50.d: Infection by Treponema pallidum transmitted from mother to fetus via the placenta, with early or late manifestations in the child.
s: Hutchinson teeth and saddle nose in the late form

A51.d: Acquired syphilis of less than one year's duration, including the primary, secondary and early latent stages, with high transmissibility.

A52.d: Acquired syphilis of more than one year's duration, with cardiovascular or neurological involvement or gummas, or in the late latent stage.

A53.d: Records syphilis without specification of stage or clinical form, such as latent syphilis of unknown duration, identified only by serology.

A54.d: Sexually transmitted infection by Neisseria gonorrhoeae, which affects the urethra, cervix, rectum, pharynx and conjunctiva.
s: Septic arthritis in the disseminated form

A55.d: Sexually transmitted infection by Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1 to L3, with lymphatic invasion.
s: Painful inguinal bubo that forms fistulas

A56.d: Sexually transmitted infections by Chlamydia trachomatis serovars D to K, frequently asymptomatic.

A57.d: Sexually transmitted infection by Haemophilus ducreyi, with painful genital ulcers and suppurative lymphadenopathy.
s: Inguinal bubo that drains through a single opening

A58.d: Chronic sexually transmitted infection by Klebsiella granulomatis, with progressive ulcerative granulomatous lesions.

A59.d: Sexually transmitted infection by the protozoan Trichomonas vaginalis, which affects the vagina and urethra.

A60.d: Genital or perianal infection by herpes simplex virus, mainly type 2, with latency in sensory ganglia and recurrences.
s: Grouped vesicles on an erythematous base

A63.n: Other predominantly sexually transmitted diseases, not elsewhere classified
A63.d: Other predominantly sexually transmitted diseases, such as anogenital warts caused by human papillomavirus.

A64.d: Records a sexually transmitted infection without a specified agent or form; management follows the syndromic approach.

A65.d: Endemic treponematosis caused by Treponema pallidum subsp. endemicum, transmitted by nonsexual contact in arid regions.

A66.d: Tropical treponematosis caused by Treponema pallidum subsp. pertenue, transmitted by contact with skin lesions, with late destruction of skin and bone.

A67.d: Treponematosis caused by Treponema carateum restricted to the skin, transmitted by contact, with pigmentation changes.

A68.d: Infection by Borrelia transmitted by lice or ticks, with recurrent febrile episodes due to antigenic variation of the agent.
s: Spirochetes on blood smear during fever

A69.d: Other spirochetal infections, including Lyme disease caused by Borrelia burgdorferi and necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis.

A70.d: Infection by Chlamydia psittaci acquired by inhaling bird secretions, causing atypical pneumonia.

A71.d: Chronic keratoconjunctivitis caused by Chlamydia trachomatis serovars A to C, with conjunctival scarring that leads to blindness.
s: Follicles on the upper tarsal conjunctiva

A74.d: Other chlamydial infections, such as inclusion conjunctivitis and neonatal pneumonia caused by Chlamydia trachomatis.

A75.d: Typhus group rickettsioses, such as louse-borne epidemic typhus and flea-borne murine typhus, with disseminated vasculitis.
s: Maculopapular rash starting on the trunk

A77.d: Spotted fever group rickettsioses transmitted by ticks, such as Rickettsia rickettsii in Brazil, with severe vasculitis.
s: Maculopapular rash starting on the wrists and ankles
Petechiae and necrosis of the extremities

A78.d: Zoonosis caused by Coxiella burnetii acquired by inhaling aerosols from infected animals, with an acute or chronic form.

A79.d: Other rickettsioses, such as scrub typhus and rickettsialpox, transmitted by mites and other vectors.

A80.d: Infection by poliovirus that destroys motor neurons of the anterior horn of the spinal cord, causing acute flaccid paralysis.
s: Respiratory failure in the bulbar form

A81.n: Atypical virus infections of central nervous system
A81.d: Neurodegenerative diseases caused by slowly progressing agents, such as prions and JC virus, with dementia and progressive neurological signs.

A82.d: Almost always fatal acute viral encephalitis caused by rabies virus, transmitted through the saliva of infected mammals.

A83.d: Encephalitis caused by mosquito-borne arboviruses, such as Japanese encephalitis, West Nile and equine encephalitides.

A84.d: Encephalitis caused by tick-borne flaviviruses, usually with a biphasic course.
s: Flaccid paralysis of the upper limbs

A85.n: Other viral encephalitis, not elsewhere classified
A85.d: Viral encephalitis due to other specified agents, such as enteroviruses and adenoviruses, not classified in the preceding categories.

A86.d: Inflammation of the brain parenchyma of presumed viral origin with no identified agent.

A87.d: Inflammation of the meninges caused by viruses, mainly enteroviruses, generally benign and self-limited.
s: CSF with lymphocytosis and normal glucose

A88.n: Other viral infections of central nervous system, not elsewhere classified
A88.d: Other viral infections of the central nervous system, such as enteroviral exanthematous fever with meningitis and epidemic vertigo.

A89.n: Unspecified viral infection of central nervous system
A89.d: Records a viral infection of the central nervous system without a specified agent or form; the presentation depends on the affected site.

A90.d: Infection by dengue virus transmitted by Aedes aegypti, with acute fever and a usually benign course.

A91.d: Severe form of dengue with plasma leakage and hemorrhage, currently called severe dengue.

A92.d: Fevers caused by mosquito-borne arboviruses, such as chikungunya, Zika, Mayaro and Oropouche.

A93.n: Other arthropod-borne viral fevers, not elsewhere classified
A93.d: Other fevers caused by arthropod-borne arboviruses, such as Oropouche transmitted by biting midges and Colorado tick fever.

A94.d: Records an arboviral fever without a specified agent, when arthropod transmission is presumed without etiological confirmation.

A95.d: Infection by yellow fever virus transmitted by mosquitoes, with severe hepatitis, hemorrhage and renal failure.

A96.d: Hemorrhagic fevers caused by rodent-borne arenaviruses, such as Lassa, Junín and Sabiá.

A98.n: Other viral haemorrhagic fevers, not elsewhere classified
A98.d: Other viral hemorrhagic fevers, such as those caused by Ebola, Marburg and hantaviruses with renal syndrome.

A99.d: Records a hemorrhagic fever of presumed viral etiology with no identified agent.

B00.d: Infection by herpes simplex virus with latency in nerve ganglia, which causes recurrent vesicular lesions on skin and mucous membranes.

B01.d: Highly contagious primary infection by varicella-zoster virus, with a generalized vesicular rash.
s: Involvement of the scalp and mucous membranes

B02.d: Reactivation of varicella-zoster virus latent in a sensory ganglion, with a vesicular eruption in a dermatome.
s: Grouped vesicles in a unilateral band

B03.d: Infection by variola virus, eradicated worldwide, with a centrifugal rash of lesions at the same stage.
s: Vesiculopustular lesions at the same stage

B04.d: Infection by mpox virus, transmitted by close contact, with skin lesions that progress from papule to crust.

B05.d: Highly contagious infection by measles virus, with a catarrhal prodrome and maculopapular rash.

B06.d: Infection by rubella virus, usually mild but teratogenic when acquired during pregnancy.

B07.d: Benign epithelial proliferations of the skin caused by human papillomavirus.
s: Keratotic papules with a rough surface

B08.n: Other viral infections characterized by skin and mucous membrane lesions, not elsewhere classified
B08.d: Other viral infections with skin and mucous membrane lesions, such as molluscum contagiosum, erythema infectiosum, exanthema subitum and hand, foot and mouth disease.
s: Fever followed by rash in exanthema subitum
Vesicles on the hands, feet and mouth

B09.n: Unspecified viral infection characterized by skin and mucous membrane lesions
B09.d: Records a viral exanthem or enanthem without a specified agent.

B15.d: Acute infection by hepatitis A virus, transmitted by the fecal-oral route, self-limited and without progression to chronicity.

B16.d: Acute infection by hepatitis B virus, transmitted sexually, parenterally or vertically, which may become chronic.

B17.d: Acute viral hepatitis caused by other agents, such as hepatitis C, D and E viruses.
s: Increased severity of hepatitis E in pregnant women

B18.d: Liver infection persisting for more than six months, mainly by hepatitis B and C viruses, which may progress to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.
s: Signs of cirrhosis in advanced stages

B19.d: Records viral hepatitis without a specified viral type.

B20.n: Human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] disease resulting in infectious and parasitic diseases
B20.d: HIV infection resulting in opportunistic infections due to depletion of CD4 T lymphocytes.

B21.n: Human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] disease resulting in malignant neoplasms
B21.d: HIV infection resulting in malignant neoplasms associated with immunodeficiency.

B22.n: Human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] disease resulting in other specified diseases
B22.d: HIV infection resulting in other specified diseases, such as encephalopathy, interstitial pneumonitis and wasting syndrome.

B23.n: Human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] disease resulting in other conditions
B23.d: HIV infection resulting in other conditions, such as acute retroviral syndrome and persistent generalized lymphadenopathy.
s: Fever and pharyngitis in acute infection

B24.d: Records HIV disease without specification of the associated manifestations.

B25.d: Infection by cytomegalovirus, usually latent, which causes end-organ disease in immunosuppressed patients and congenital infection.

B26.d: Infection by mumps virus, transmitted by droplets, with inflammation of the salivary glands.
s: Painful enlargement of the parotid glands

B27.d: Infection mainly by Epstein-Barr virus, with reactive lymphocyte proliferation, common in adolescents and young adults.

B30.d: Inflammation of the conjunctiva caused by viruses, mainly adenovirus, highly contagious.

B33.n: Other viral diseases, not elsewhere classified
B33.d: Other specified viral diseases not elsewhere classified, such as epidemic myalgia, Ross River fever and viral carditis.

B34.d: Records a viral infection of unspecified site, with or without an identified agent; the clinical picture depends on the virus.

B35.d: Superficial infections of the skin, hair and nails by dermatophyte fungi that digest keratin.
s: Patchy hair loss on the scalp

B36.d: Superficial mycoses caused by nondermatophyte fungi, such as pityriasis versicolor, tinea nigra and piedra.
s: Hypo- or hyperpigmented patches with fine scaling

B37.d: Opportunistic Candida infection that affects the skin, mucous membranes and, in immunosuppressed patients, deep organs.
s: Removable whitish plaques in the mouth

B38.d: Systemic mycosis caused by Coccidioides, acquired by inhaling soil spores in arid regions, with a predominantly pulmonary form.

B39.d: Systemic mycosis caused by Histoplasma capsulatum, acquired by inhaling spores from bird and bat droppings.

B40.d: Mycosis caused by Blastomyces dermatitidis, acquired by inhalation, with pulmonary, cutaneous and bone involvement.

B41.d: Systemic mycosis caused by Paracoccidioides, endemic in Latin America, acquired by inhalation during rural activities.

B42.d: Subcutaneous mycosis caused by Sporothrix, acquired by traumatic inoculation or scratches from infected cats.
s: Nodule or ulcer at the inoculation site
Chain of nodules along the lymphatic path

B43.d: Chronic subcutaneous mycoses caused by dematiaceous fungi, forming verrucous lesions or abscesses after traumatic inoculation.
s: Verrucous plaques on the lower limbs

B44.d: Aspergillus infection, which may be allergic, colonize cavities or invade tissues in immunosuppressed patients.
s: Bronchospasm and eosinophilia in the allergic form

B45.d: Cryptococcus infection acquired by inhalation, with tropism for the central nervous system in immunosuppressed patients.
s: Positive cryptococcal antigen or India ink

B46.d: Angioinvasive, necrotizing infections caused by fungi of the order Mucorales, in patients with uncontrolled diabetes and immunosuppressed patients.
s: Black eschar on the palate or nose

B47.d: Chronic subcutaneous infection caused by fungi or actinomycetes, with swelling, sinus tracts and grains, usually in the feet.

B48.d: Other specified mycoses, such as lobomycosis, rhinosporidiosis and infections by rare opportunistic fungi.

B49.d: Records a fungal infection without a specified agent.

B50.d: Malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum, the most severe form, with high parasitemia and sequestration of red blood cells in the microcirculation.
s: Cerebral malaria with seizures and coma

B51.d: Malaria caused by Plasmodium vivax, the most common in Brazil, with hepatic hypnozoites responsible for relapses.

B52.d: Malaria caused by Plasmodium malariae, with quartan fever and chronic low-grade parasitemia.

B53.d: Other parasitologically confirmed forms of malaria, such as those caused by Plasmodium ovale and Plasmodium knowlesi.

B54.d: Malaria diagnosed clinically without parasitological confirmation of the species.

B55.d: Leishmania infection transmitted by sand flies, with visceral, cutaneous and mucocutaneous forms.
s: Destructive lesion of the nasal mucosa
Prolonged fever in the visceral form

B56.d: Trypanosoma brucei infection transmitted by the tsetse fly, with a hemolymphatic phase and a meningoencephalitic phase.

B57.d: Trypanosoma cruzi infection transmitted by triatomine bugs, orally or vertically, with an acute phase and chronic cardiomyopathy or mega-organs.
s: Romaña sign in the acute phase
Right bundle branch block and arrhythmias

B58.d: Toxoplasma gondii infection, usually asymptomatic, severe in the congenital form and in immunosuppressed patients.
s: Hydrocephalus and calcifications in the congenital form

B59.d: Pneumonia caused by the fungus Pneumocystis jirovecii in immunosuppressed patients, especially those with HIV and low CD4 count.

B60.n: Other protozoal diseases, not elsewhere classified
B60.d: Other protozoal diseases, such as babesiosis, acanthamebiasis and Naegleria infection.
s: Fulminant meningoencephalitis after swimming in fresh water

B64.d: Records a protozoal disease without a specified agent.

B65.d: Schistosoma infection acquired by cercarial penetration of the skin, with granulomas around the eggs and fibrosis.
s: Fever and eosinophilia in the acute phase

B66.d: Other trematode infections, such as fascioliasis and clonorchiasis, acquired by eating contaminated vegetables or fish.

B67.d: Infection by the larval form of Echinococcus, with hydatid cysts mainly in the liver and lung.
s: Cough and hemoptysis with pulmonary cysts
Cyst with daughter vesicles on imaging

B68.d: Intestinal infection by the adult form of Taenia solium or Taenia saginata, acquired from undercooked meat.

B69.d: Infection by the larval form of Taenia solium after ingestion of eggs, with cysts in the nervous system, muscles and eyes.

B70.d: Diphyllobothrium infection acquired from raw fish, or infection by the Spirometra larva in sparganosis.
s: Megaloblastic anemia due to B12 deficiency

B71.d: Other cestode infections, such as hymenolepiasis and dipylidiasis.
s: Eggs or proglottids in the stool

B72.d: Infection by the Guinea worm, Dracunculus medinensis, acquired by drinking water containing infected copepods.
s: Painful blister on the lower limb

B73.d: Filariasis caused by Onchocerca volvulus, transmitted by blackflies, with microfilariae in the skin and eyes.

B74.d: Infection by filariae such as Wuchereria bancrofti, transmitted by mosquitoes, with chronic lymphatic obstruction.

B75.d: Trichinella infection acquired from raw or undercooked meat, with larvae encysted in skeletal muscle.

B76.d: Infection by hookworms that penetrate the skin and attach to the small intestine, causing chronic blood loss.

B77.d: Ascaris lumbricoides infection acquired by ingesting eggs, with a larval pulmonary cycle and adult worms in the intestine.
s: Intestinal obstruction by a worm bolus

B78.d: Strongyloides stercoralis infection, with autoinfection and a risk of hyperinfection in immunosuppressed patients.

B79.d: Trichuris trichiura infection of the colon, acquired by ingesting eggs.

B80.d: Enterobius vermicularis infection, common in children, with nocturnal migration of the females to the perianal region.
s: Eggs on perianal adhesive tape test

B81.n: Other intestinal helminthiases, not elsewhere classified
B81.d: Other intestinal helminthiases, such as abdominal angiostrongyliasis, intestinal capillariasis and trichostrongyliasis.

B82.d: Records intestinal parasitism without an identified agent.

B83.d: Other helminthiases, such as visceral larva migrans, gnathostomiasis and meningeal angiostrongyliasis.

B85.d: Infestation by head, body or pubic lice, which feed on human blood.

B86.d: Skin infestation by the mite Sarcoptes scabiei, transmitted by contact, with a hypersensitivity reaction.
s: Burrows and papules in the interdigital spaces
Lesions on wrists, axillae and genitals

B87.d: Infestation of tissues or cavities by fly larvae, in wounds or by penetration of the skin.

B88.d: Other infestations, such as tungiasis, cutaneous larva migrans and acariasis.
s: Papule with a central black dot on the foot in tungiasis

B89.d: Records a parasitic disease without a specified agent or type.

B90.d: Records residual conditions after cured tuberculosis, such as fibrosis, bronchiectasis and deformities, used when active disease is no longer present.

B91.d: Records permanent motor deficits after poliomyelitis, including post-polio syndrome.

B92.d: Records permanent disabilities after treated leprosy, due to nerve damage.

B94.n: Sequelae of other and unspecified infectious and parasitic diseases
B94.d: Records sequelae of other infectious and parasitic diseases, such as trachoma, viral encephalitis and viral hepatitis, when the infection is no longer active.

B95.n: Streptococcus and staphylococcus as the cause of diseases classified to other chapters
B95.d: Supplementary code that identifies streptococci and staphylococci as agents of diseases classified in other chapters.

B96.n: Other bacterial agents as the cause of diseases classified to other chapters
B96.d: Supplementary code that identifies other bacteria, such as Escherichia coli, Klebsiella and Pseudomonas, as agents of diseases classified in other chapters.

B97.n: Viral agents as the cause of diseases classified to other chapters
B97.d: Supplementary code that identifies viruses as agents of diseases classified in other chapters, such as adenovirus and respiratory syncytial virus.

B99.d: Records an infectious disease without a specified agent or site.

C00.d: Carcinoma, usually squamous cell, of the lip, especially the lower lip, associated with chronic sun exposure and smoking.

C01.n: Malignant neoplasm of base of tongue
C01.d: Squamous cell carcinoma of the base of the tongue, in the oropharynx, associated with tobacco, alcohol and human papillomavirus.

C02.n: Malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified parts of tongue
C02.d: Carcinoma of the oral tongue and other portions, mainly squamous cell, related to smoking and alcohol use.
s: Indurated ulcer on the lateral border of the tongue

C03.d: Carcinoma of the gum, usually squamous cell, which may invade the alveolar bone.
s: Ulcerated or exophytic lesion on the gum

C04.n: Malignant neoplasm of floor of mouth
C04.d: Squamous cell carcinoma of the floor of the mouth, strongly associated with smoking and alcohol use.
s: Ulcer on the floor of the mouth

C05.d: Malignant neoplasm of the hard or soft palate, including squamous cell carcinoma and minor salivary gland tumors.

C06.n: Malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified parts of mouth
C06.d: Malignant neoplasm of other regions of the mouth, such as the buccal mucosa and retromolar area, predominantly squamous cell carcinoma.
s: Persistent ulcer of the oral mucosa

C07.d: Malignant neoplasm of the parotid gland, such as mucoepidermoid and adenoid cystic carcinoma.

C08.n: Malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified major salivary glands
C08.d: Malignant neoplasm of the submandibular and sublingual glands.

C09.d: Carcinoma of the palatine tonsil, often related to human papillomavirus, with early cervical metastasis.

C10.d: Squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx, associated with human papillomavirus, smoking and alcohol use.

C11.d: Carcinoma of the nasopharynx, associated with Epstein-Barr virus, with early lymph node spread.

C12.d: Squamous cell carcinoma of the piriform sinus, in the hypopharynx, often diagnosed late.

C13.d: Squamous cell carcinoma of the hypopharynx, linked to tobacco and alcohol, with a guarded prognosis.

C14.n: Malignant neoplasm of other and ill-defined sites in the lip, oral cavity and pharynx
C14.d: Records a malignant neoplasm of the lip, oral cavity and pharynx with an overlapping or ill-defined site.

C15.d: Malignant neoplasm of the esophagus, such as squamous cell carcinoma linked to tobacco and alcohol and adenocarcinoma linked to Barrett's esophagus.
s: Progressive dysphagia to solids and then liquids

C16.d: Malignant neoplasm of the stomach, predominantly adenocarcinoma, associated with Helicobacter pylori and atrophic gastritis.

C17.d: Malignant neoplasm of the small intestine, such as adenocarcinoma, neuroendocrine tumor, lymphoma and GIST.

C18.d: Adenocarcinoma of the colon, usually arising from adenomatous polyps.

C19.d: Adenocarcinoma of the transition between the sigmoid colon and the rectum.

C20.d: Adenocarcinoma of the rectum, whose treatment considers neoadjuvant therapy and sphincter preservation.

C21.n: Malignant neoplasm of anus and anal canal
C21.d: Malignant neoplasm of the anus and anal canal, usually squamous cell carcinoma associated with human papillomavirus.

C22.n: Malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile ducts
C22.d: Primary malignant neoplasm of the liver, such as hepatocellular carcinoma arising in cirrhosis and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
s: Nodule with arterial enhancement and washout on imaging

C23.d: Adenocarcinoma of the gallbladder, associated with chronic cholelithiasis and porcelain gallbladder, usually diagnosed late.

C24.n: Malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified parts of biliary tract
C24.d: Malignant neoplasm of the extrahepatic bile ducts and the ampulla of Vater, mainly cholangiocarcinoma.

C25.d: Malignant neoplasm of the pancreas, mainly ductal adenocarcinoma, diagnosed late and with high lethality.
s: Epigastric pain radiating to the back

C26.n: Malignant neoplasm of other and ill-defined digestive organs
C26.d: Records a malignant neoplasm of the digestive system with an overlapping or ill-defined site.

C30.n: Malignant neoplasm of nasal cavity and middle ear
C30.d: Malignant neoplasm of the nasal cavity or middle ear, including squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma.

C31.d: Malignant neoplasm of the paranasal sinuses, especially the maxillary sinus, associated with occupational exposure to wood dust and nickel.

C32.d: Squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx, strongly associated with smoking.

C33.d: Rare malignant neoplasm of the trachea, such as squamous cell and adenoid cystic carcinoma.

C34.n: Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung
C34.d: Malignant neoplasm of the bronchi and lungs, such as adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma and small cell carcinoma, associated with smoking.

C37.d: Malignant epithelial neoplasm of the thymus, located in the anterior mediastinum, associated with paraneoplastic syndromes.

C38.n: Malignant neoplasm of heart, mediastinum and pleura
C38.d: Malignant neoplasm of the heart, mediastinum or pleura, including sarcomas, germ cell tumors and lymphomas.

C39.n: Malignant neoplasm of other and ill-defined sites in the respiratory system and intrathoracic organs
C39.d: Records a malignant neoplasm of the respiratory system or intrathoracic organs with an overlapping or ill-defined site.

C40.n: Malignant neoplasm of bone and articular cartilage of limbs
C40.d: Primary malignant neoplasm of the long bones of the limbs, such as osteosarcoma and Ewing sarcoma, more common in young people.
s: Lytic or blastic lesion on X-ray

C41.n: Malignant neoplasm of bone and articular cartilage of other and unspecified sites
C41.d: Primary malignant neoplasm of the bones of the skull, spine, ribs and pelvis, such as chondrosarcoma and chordoma.

C43.d: Malignant neoplasm of cutaneous melanocytes, associated with intermittent sun exposure and with high metastatic potential.

C44.d: Non-melanoma malignant neoplasms of the skin, mainly basal cell and squamous cell carcinoma, associated with sun exposure.

C45.d: Malignant neoplasm of the serous membranes, especially the pleura, strongly associated with asbestos exposure.

C46.d: Vascular neoplasm associated with human herpesvirus 8, common in people with HIV and immunosuppressed people.
s: Violaceous macules or nodules on the skin

C47.n: Malignant neoplasm of peripheral nerves and autonomic nervous system
C47.d: Malignant neoplasm of the peripheral nerves and autonomic nervous system, such as malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor and neuroblastoma.

C48.n: Malignant neoplasm of retroperitoneum and peritoneum
C48.d: Malignant neoplasm of the retroperitoneum and peritoneum, such as retroperitoneal liposarcoma and primary peritoneal carcinoma.

C49.n: Malignant neoplasm of other connective and soft tissue
C49.d: Soft tissue sarcomas, such as those of muscle, fat, tendons and vessels, outside the retroperitoneum.

C50.d: Malignant neoplasm of the breast, mainly ductal or lobular carcinoma, classified by hormone receptors and HER2.

C51.d: Malignant neoplasm of the vulva, usually squamous cell carcinoma, associated with human papillomavirus or lichen sclerosus.

C52.d: Rare primary malignant neoplasm of the vagina, usually squamous cell carcinoma.

C53.d: Malignant neoplasm of the uterine cervix, caused by persistent infection with oncogenic human papillomavirus.

C54.d: Malignant neoplasm of the uterine corpus, mainly endometrial adenocarcinoma, associated with estrogen excess and obesity.

C55.n: Malignant neoplasm of uterus, part unspecified
C55.d: Records a malignant neoplasm of the uterus without distinction between cervix and corpus.

C56.d: Malignant neoplasm of the ovary, mainly serous epithelial carcinoma, often diagnosed at an advanced stage.

C57.n: Malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified female genital organs
C57.d: Malignant neoplasm of other female genital organs, such as the fallopian tubes, ligaments and parametrium.

C58.d: Malignant trophoblastic neoplasm, mainly choriocarcinoma, producing chorionic gonadotropin.

C60.d: Squamous cell carcinoma of the penis, associated with phimosis, poor hygiene and human papillomavirus.
s: Ulcerated or exophytic lesion on the glans or foreskin

C61.d: Adenocarcinoma of the prostate, most common in older men, often slowly progressive.
s: Hard nodule on digital rectal examination

C62.d: Malignant neoplasm of the testis, mainly germ cell tumors in young men.
s: Elevated AFP, beta-hCG and LDH markers

C63.n: Malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified male genital organs
C63.d: Malignant neoplasm of other male genital organs, such as the epididymis, spermatic cord and scrotum.

C64.n: Malignant neoplasm of kidney, except renal pelvis
C64.d: Malignant neoplasm of the renal parenchyma, mainly clear cell carcinoma, often an incidental finding.

C65.d: Urothelial carcinoma of the renal pelvis, associated with smoking.

C66.d: Urothelial carcinoma of the ureter, associated with smoking.

C67.d: Malignant neoplasm of the bladder, mainly urothelial carcinoma, strongly associated with smoking and aromatic amines.

C68.n: Malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified urinary organs
C68.d: Malignant neoplasm of other urinary organs, such as the urethra and urachus.

C69.n: Malignant neoplasm of eye and adnexa
C69.d: Malignant neoplasm of the eye and adnexa, such as retinoblastoma in children and uveal melanoma in adults.

C70.d: Malignant neoplasm of the meninges, rare, including malignant meningioma and meningeal sarcomas.

C71.d: Primary malignant neoplasm of the brain, mainly gliomas such as glioblastoma.

C72.n: Malignant neoplasm of spinal cord, cranial nerves and other parts of central nervous system
C72.d: Malignant neoplasm of the spinal cord, cranial nerves and other parts of the central nervous system, such as ependymomas and optic nerve gliomas.

C73.d: Malignant neoplasm of the thyroid, mainly papillary carcinoma, usually with a good prognosis.

C74.d: Malignant neoplasm of the adrenal gland, such as adrenocortical carcinoma and malignant pheochromocytoma, which may produce hormones.

C75.n: Malignant neoplasm of other endocrine glands and related structures
C75.d: Malignant neoplasm of other endocrine glands, such as the parathyroid, pituitary, pineal gland and carotid bodies.

C76.n: Malignant neoplasm of other and ill-defined sites
C76.d: Records a malignant neoplasm in an ill-defined anatomical region, such as the head, thorax, abdomen or limbs, with no determined organ of origin.

C77.n: Secondary and unspecified malignant neoplasm of lymph nodes
C77.d: Records lymph node involvement by a metastatic malignant neoplasm or one of unspecified origin.

C78.n: Secondary malignant neoplasm of respiratory and digestive organs
C78.d: Metastases of malignant neoplasm to the lungs, pleura, mediastinum, liver, peritoneum and other digestive organs.

C79.n: Secondary malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified sites
C79.d: Metastases of malignant neoplasm to other sites, such as the brain, bones, adrenal glands and skin.

C80.n: Malignant neoplasm, without specification of site
C80.d: Records a malignant neoplasm with no identified primary site, including carcinoma of unknown primary site.

C81.d: Lymphoma with Reed-Sternberg cells, with contiguous spread between lymph node chains and a good prognosis.
s: Fever, night sweats and weight loss
Lymph node pain after drinking alcohol

C82.d: Indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma of germinal center B cells, with translocation t(14;18) and BCL2 expression.

C83.d: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma with a diffuse pattern, mainly diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, with rapid growth.

C84.d: Mature T-cell lymphomas, such as mycosis fungoides, Sézary syndrome and peripheral T-cell lymphomas.
s: Scaly erythematous plaques in mycosis fungoides

C85.n: Other and unspecified types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma
C85.d: Records non-Hodgkin lymphoma of other types or of unspecified type.
s: Fever, night sweats and weight loss

C88.d: Malignant immunoproliferative diseases with monoclonal immunoglobulin production, such as Waldenström macroglobulinemia and heavy chain diseases.

C90.n: Multiple myeloma and malignant plasma cell neoplasms
C90.d: Clonal proliferation of plasma cells in the bone marrow with monoclonal protein production and organ damage.

C91.d: Leukemias of the lymphoid lineage, acute as in childhood lymphoblastic leukemia or chronic as in chronic lymphocytic leukemia.
s: Lymphocytosis or blasts in the blood

C92.d: Leukemias of the myeloid lineage, such as acute myeloid leukemia and chronic myeloid leukemia with the Philadelphia chromosome.
s: Massive splenomegaly in the chronic form
Myeloblasts or leukocytosis with left shift

C93.d: Leukemias of the monocytic lineage, acute or chronic, such as chronic myelomonocytic leukemia.

C94.n: Other leukemias of specified cell type
C94.d: Other leukemias of specified cell type, such as erythroleukemia and acute megakaryoblastic leukemia.
s: Blasts in the blood or marrow

C95.d: Records leukemia with no specified cell type.

C96.n: Other and unspecified malignant neoplasms of lymphoid, hematopoietic and related tissue
C96.d: Other malignant neoplasms of lymphoid and hematopoietic tissue, such as multisystem Langerhans cell histiocytosis and histiocytic sarcoma.

C97.n: Malignant neoplasms of independent (primary) multiple sites
C97.d: Code used when there are two or more independent primary malignant neoplasms, each also coded separately.

D00.n: Carcinoma in situ of oral cavity, esophagus and stomach
D00.d: Epithelial neoplasm confined to the epithelium, without invasion of the basement membrane, in the mouth, esophagus or stomach.

D01.n: Carcinoma in situ of other and unspecified digestive organs
D01.d: Carcinoma confined to the epithelium in other digestive organs, such as the colon, rectum, anus and liver.

D02.n: Carcinoma in situ of middle ear and respiratory system
D02.d: Carcinoma confined to the epithelium in the middle ear, larynx, trachea, bronchi or lung.

D03.d: Melanoma limited to the epidermis, without dermal invasion, with an excellent prognosis after complete excision.
s: Slow growth in a sun-exposed area

D04.d: Squamous cell carcinoma confined to the epidermis, also called Bowen disease.

D05.d: Breast carcinoma confined to the ducts or lobules, without stromal invasion.

D06.n: Carcinoma in situ of cervix uteri
D06.d: High-grade intraepithelial lesion of the uterine cervix, a precursor of cancer, caused by human papillomavirus.

D07.n: Carcinoma in situ of other and unspecified genital organs
D07.d: Carcinoma confined to the epithelium in other genital organs, such as the vulva, vagina, penis and prostate.
s: Penile lesion in erythroplasia of Queyrat

D09.n: Carcinoma in situ of other and unspecified sites
D09.d: Carcinoma confined to the epithelium in other sites, such as the bladder, eye and thyroid, or of unspecified site.
s: Hematuria in bladder carcinoma in situ

D10.n: Benign neoplasm of mouth and pharynx
D10.d: Benign neoplasm of the mouth and pharynx, such as papilloma, fibroma, pleomorphic adenoma of a minor gland and polyps.

D11.n: Benign neoplasm of major salivary glands
D11.d: Benign tumor of the parotid, submandibular or sublingual gland, most commonly pleomorphic adenoma, with slow growth.
s: Painless, mobile nodule in the parotid region

D12.n: Benign neoplasm of colon, rectum, anus and anal canal
D12.d: Benign epithelial or mesenchymal proliferation of the large intestine, especially adenomatous polyps with malignant potential.
s: Iron deficiency anemia in larger lesions

D13.n: Benign neoplasm of other and ill-defined parts of digestive system
D13.d: Benign tumor of the esophagus, stomach, small intestine, liver, biliary tract or pancreas, such as adenomas, leiomyomas and hemangiomas.
s: Incidental finding on imaging or endoscopy

D14.n: Benign neoplasm of middle ear and respiratory system
D14.d: Benign tumor of the middle ear, nasal cavity, paranasal sinuses, larynx, trachea or lung, such as papillomas and hamartomas.

D15.n: Benign neoplasm of other and unspecified intrathoracic organs
D15.d: Benign tumor of the thymus, heart, mediastinum or other thoracic organs, such as noninvasive thymoma and atrial myxoma.
s: Dyspnea or cough due to compression
Murmur or embolic symptoms in myxoma

D16.n: Benign neoplasm of bone and articular cartilage
D16.d: Benign bone or cartilage lesion, such as osteochondroma, enchondroma, osteoid osteoma and giant cell tumor.
s: Night pain relieved by NSAIDs in osteoid osteoma

D17.d: Benign tumor formed by mature adipocytes, usually subcutaneous, mobile and soft in consistency.

D18.d: Benign malformation or proliferation of blood or lymphatic vessels, common in the skin in childhood and in organs such as the liver.
s: Reddish or violaceous patch or nodule
Growth in the first months followed by involution

D19.d: Benign tumor arising from the mesothelium of the pleura, peritoneum or pericardium, such as adenomatoid tumor and solitary fibrous tumor.
s: Chest pain or dyspnea in large lesions

D20.n: Benign neoplasm of soft tissue of retroperitoneum and peritoneum
D20.d: Benign soft tissue tumor located in the retroperitoneum or peritoneum, such as lipoma, schwannoma or leiomyoma.

D21.n: Other benign neoplasms of connective and other soft tissue
D21.d: Benign tumor of fibrous, muscle, peripheral nerve or other soft tissue, such as fibroma and cutaneous leiomyoma.

D22.d: Benign proliferation of melanocytes in the skin, congenital or acquired, forming pigmented macules or papules.

D23.d: Non-melanocytic benign skin tumor, such as seborrheic keratosis, dermatofibroma and adnexal tumors.
s: Warty, stuck-on appearance in seborrheic keratosis

D24.d: Benign breast tumor, especially fibroadenoma in young women and intraductal papilloma.
s: Peak in women aged 15 to 35 years

D25.d: Estrogen-dependent benign tumor of uterine smooth muscle, very common in the reproductive years.

D26.d: Benign uterine tumor not arising from the myometrium, such as endometrial polyps and adenomyomas.

D27.d: Benign ovarian tumor, such as serous or mucinous cystadenoma and mature cystic teratoma.

D28.n: Benign neoplasm of other and unspecified female genital organs
D28.d: Benign tumor of the vulva, vagina, fallopian tubes or other female genital organs, or of an unspecified genital organ.

D29.n: Benign neoplasm of male genital organs
D29.d: Benign tumor of the penis, prostate, testis, epididymis or scrotum, such as adenomatoid tumor of the epididymis.
s: Finding on physical examination or ultrasound

D30.d: Benign tumor of the kidney, renal pelvis, ureter, bladder or urethra, such as angiomyolipoma and oncocytoma.

D31.n: Benign neoplasm of eye and adnexa
D31.d: Benign tumor of the eyeball, conjunctiva, orbit or lacrimal gland, such as choroidal nevus and orbital cavernous hemangioma.

D32.d: Benign tumor of the meninges, represented mainly by meningioma, slow-growing and more common in women.
s: Extra-axial lesion with dural tail on MRI

D33.n: Benign neoplasm of brain and other parts of central nervous system
D33.d: Benign tumor of the brain, cranial nerves or spinal cord, such as vestibular schwannoma and some low-grade tumors.
s: Unilateral hearing loss and tinnitus in vestibular schwannoma

D34.d: Benign thyroid tumor, especially follicular adenoma, presenting as a solitary nodule.
s: Anterior neck nodule that moves with swallowing
Fine-needle aspiration with benign or follicular pattern

D35.n: Benign neoplasm of other and unspecified endocrine glands
D35.d: Benign tumor of the adrenal, pituitary, parathyroid or other endocrine glands, functioning or not.
s: Hormone hypersecretion depending on the gland

D36.n: Benign neoplasm of other and unspecified sites
D36.d: Benign tumor of an unlisted or unspecified site, such as tumors of peripheral nerves and lymph nodes.

D37.n: Neoplasm of uncertain or unknown behavior of oral cavity and digestive organs
D37.d: Tumor of the oral cavity or digestive tract whose biological behavior cannot be determined by histology, such as GIST and borderline neuroendocrine tumors.
s: Abdominal mass or submucosal lesion on endoscopy

D38.n: Neoplasm of uncertain or unknown behavior of middle ear and respiratory and intrathoracic organs
D38.d: Tumor of the larynx, trachea, lung, pleura, thymus or middle ear of uncertain biological behavior, such as typical carcinoid and thymoma.

D39.n: Neoplasm of uncertain or unknown behavior of female genital organs
D39.d: Tumor of the ovary, uterus or placenta of uncertain behavior, such as borderline ovarian tumors and invasive hydatidiform mole.

D40.n: Neoplasm of uncertain or unknown behavior of male genital organs
D40.d: Tumor of the prostate, testis or other male genital organs whose benign or malignant course is not predictable.

D41.n: Neoplasm of uncertain or unknown behavior of urinary organs
D41.d: Tumor of the kidney, bladder, ureter or urethra of uncertain behavior, such as urothelial neoplasms of low malignant potential.

D42.n: Neoplasm of uncertain or unknown behavior of meninges
D42.d: Meningeal tumor whose behavior cannot be determined, such as atypical meningioma and hemangiopericytoma.

D43.n: Neoplasm of uncertain or unknown behavior of brain and central nervous system
D43.d: Tumor of the brain, spinal cord or cranial nerves of uncertain behavior, such as some glial tumors and ependymomas.

D44.n: Neoplasm of uncertain or unknown behavior of endocrine glands
D44.d: Tumor of the thyroid, adrenal, pituitary, parathyroid or paraganglia of uncertain behavior, such as pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma.
s: Paroxysmal hypertension with headache, sweating and palpitations
Visual changes due to a pituitary lesion

D45.d: Clonal myeloproliferative neoplasm, almost always with a JAK2 mutation, that increases red cell mass independently of erythropoietin.

D46.d: Clonal bone marrow neoplasms with ineffective hematopoiesis and dysplasia, which cause cytopenias and may progress to acute leukemia.

D47.n: Other neoplasms of uncertain or unknown behavior of lymphoid, hematopoietic and related tissue
D47.d: Lymphoid or myeloid neoplasms of uncertain behavior, such as essential thrombocythemia, myelofibrosis and monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance.

D48.n: Neoplasm of uncertain or unknown behavior of other and unspecified sites
D48.d: Tumor of uncertain behavior in bone, soft tissue, skin, breast or an unspecified site, such as desmoid tumor and mastocytosis.

D50.d: Microcytic anemia due to insufficient iron stores, usually from chronic blood loss, low intake or malabsorption.

D51.d: Megaloblastic anemia due to lack of cobalamin, often from pernicious anemia, which also damages the nervous system.
s: Paresthesias and loss of vibration sense
Low B12 and elevated methylmalonic acid

D52.d: Megaloblastic anemia due to lack of folic acid, linked to poor diet, alcoholism, pregnancy or antifolate drugs.

D53.d: Anemias due to nutritional deficiency of protein, copper, vitamin C or other nutrients, other than iron, B12 and folate.
s: Anemia in the setting of malnutrition

D55.d: Hemolytic anemia due to a defect in red cell enzymes, such as G6PD or pyruvate kinase deficiency.
s: Hemolytic crises after infection, drugs or fava beans

D56.d: Hereditary defect in the synthesis of alpha or beta globin chains, causing microcytic anemia and hemolysis of variable severity.

D57.d: Hemoglobinopathy caused by hemoglobin S, which polymerizes under hypoxia, deforms the red cell and causes hemolysis and vaso-occlusion.

D58.d: Hereditary hemolytic anemias due to membrane defects, such as spherocytosis and elliptocytosis.

D59.d: Acquired red cell destruction by an immune, microangiopathic, infectious or toxic mechanism, or paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria.
s: Positive direct Coombs test in autoimmune forms

D60.d: Selective suppression of erythroid precursors in the marrow, associated with thymoma, autoimmunity, parvovirus B19 or drugs.
s: Absence of erythroblasts in the marrow

D61.d: Bone marrow failure with hypocellularity and pancytopenia, idiopathic, congenital or due to drugs, radiation or viruses.

D62.d: Anemia due to sudden loss of a large volume of blood, with hypovolemia before the full drop in hemoglobin.
s: Falling hemoglobin over the following hours

D63.n: Anemia in chronic diseases classified elsewhere
D63.d: Anemia secondary to chronic inflammation, cancer or kidney disease, with hepcidin-mediated iron blockade or lack of erythropoietin.

D64.d: Anemias of other or unspecified causes, such as sideroblastic anemias and those without a completed etiological workup.

D65.d: Systemic activation of coagulation with consumption of platelets and factors, producing microthrombi and bleeding, secondary to sepsis, trauma or cancer.
s: Diffuse bleeding from puncture sites and mucosa

D66.d: Hemophilia A, an X-linked disease with lack of factor VIII, causing joint and muscle bleeding.

D67.d: Hemophilia B, an X-linked hereditary deficiency of factor IX, with a bleeding picture similar to that of hemophilia A.
s: Prolonged bleeding after surgery or tooth extraction

D68.d: Other hereditary or acquired coagulation disorders, such as von Willebrand disease, thrombophilias and vitamin K deficiency.

D69.d: Bleeding due to platelet or vessel abnormalities, such as immune thrombocytopenic purpura and vasculitides.

D70.d: Marked reduction in neutrophils, congenital, due to chemotherapy or a drug reaction, with a high risk of severe infection.

D71.d: Defects of neutrophil function, such as chronic granulomatous disease, that impair the killing of microorganisms.

D72.n: Other disorders of white blood cells
D72.d: White blood cell abnormalities not classified elsewhere, such as reactive leukocytosis, eosinophilia and lymphopenia.

D73.d: Diseases of the spleen, such as hyposplenism, hypersplenism, splenic infarction, cyst and abscess.

D74.d: Excess of hemoglobin with oxidized iron, unable to carry oxygen, congenital or induced by drugs and nitrites.
s: Cyanosis that does not improve with oxygen
Elevated methemoglobin on blood gas analysis

D75.n: Other diseases of blood and blood-forming organs
D75.d: Other hematological abnormalities, such as secondary polycythemia and reactive thrombocytosis.
s: Elevated hematocrit due to chronic hypoxia

D76.n: Certain diseases involving lymphoreticular tissue and reticulohistiocytic system
D76.d: Diseases of histiocytes and lymphoreticular tissue, such as hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis and Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
s: Markedly elevated ferritin in the hemophagocytic form

D77.n: Other disorders of blood and blood-forming organs in diseases classified elsewhere
D77.d: Hematological abnormalities secondary to diseases in other chapters, such as splenomegaly in schistosomiasis; the presentation depends on the underlying disease.

D80.d: Primary immunodeficiencies with failure of antibody production, such as X-linked agammaglobulinemia and IgA deficiency.

D81.d: Primary immunodeficiencies with T- and B-cell defects, such as severe combined immunodeficiency.
s: Severe infections in the first year of life
Chronic diarrhea and poor weight gain

D82.n: Immunodeficiency associated with other major defects
D82.d: Immunodeficiencies linked to syndromes with other malformations, such as Wiskott-Aldrich, DiGeorge and ataxia-telangiectasia.
s: Hypocalcemia and heart disease in DiGeorge

D83.d: Primary immunodeficiency with hypogammaglobulinemia and poor vaccine response, usually with onset in young adulthood.
s: Low IgG with low IgA or IgM

D84.d: Other immunodeficiencies, such as complement deficiencies and unspecified immune defects.

D86.d: Systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause with noncaseating granulomas, especially in the lungs and lymph nodes.

D89.n: Other disorders involving the immune mechanism, not elsewhere classified
D89.d: Other immune system abnormalities, such as cryoglobulinemia, polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia and mast cell activation syndrome.
s: Flushing and urticaria in mast cell activation

E00.d: Cretinism due to maternal iodine deficiency during pregnancy, with fetal hypothyroidism and irreversible neurological damage.

E01.n: Iodine-deficiency-related thyroid disorders and allied conditions
E01.d: Endemic goitre and hypothyroidism due to insufficient iodine intake in populations of deprived areas.
s: Elevated TSH with low or normal T4

E02.d: Elevated TSH with normal thyroid hormones, attributed to low dietary iodine supply.
s: Elevated TSH and normal free T4

E03.d: Insufficient production of thyroid hormones, most commonly due to Hashimoto autoimmune thyroiditis.
s: High TSH with low free T4

E04.d: Thyroid enlargement without hormonal hyperfunction, diffuse or nodular, often asymptomatic.

E05.d: Excess circulating thyroid hormones, with Graves disease as the most frequent cause.
s: Suppressed TSH with elevated free T4

E06.d: Inflammation of the thyroid of autoimmune, infectious or post-viral cause, which may run through phases of thyrotoxicosis and hypothyroidism.
s: Neck pain in the subacute form
Reduced iodine uptake in the inflammatory phase
Anti-TPO antibodies in the autoimmune form

E07.d: Residual category for thyroid abnormalities not classified in the previous ones, such as calcitonin hypersecretion and glandular hemorrhage.

E10.d: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells leading to absolute insulin deficiency.
s: Usual onset in childhood or adolescence

E11.d: Chronic hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with progressive beta-cell failure.
s: Fasting glucose greater than or equal to 126
Glycated hemoglobin greater than or equal to 6.5

E12.d: Diabetes associated with prior protein-energy malnutrition, described in low-income populations; an entity of controversial definition.
s: Hyperglycemia with little tendency to ketosis

E13.d: Diabetes of a defined cause distinct from types 1 and 2, such as MODY, exocrine pancreatic disease or secondary to endocrinopathies.

E14.d: Diagnosed hyperglycemia without a recorded etiological classification, used when the type has not been determined.

E15.d: Decreased level of consciousness due to severe hypoglycemia in a patient without diabetes, including toxic and endocrine causes.
s: Rapid reversal with correction of blood glucose

E16.n: Other disorders of pancreatic internal secretion
E16.d: Abnormalities in the secretion of pancreatic islet hormones, including hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycemia and tumors such as insulinoma and gastrinoma.

E20.d: Deficient parathyroid hormone secretion leading to hypocalcemia, the most common cause being surgical injury to the parathyroid glands.
s: Tetany with Chvostek and Trousseau signs

E21.n: Hyperparathyroidism and other disorders of parathyroid gland
E21.d: Excess parathyroid hormone, primary due to parathyroid adenoma or secondary to chronic kidney disease and vitamin D deficiency.
s: Hypercalcemia with elevated PTH in the primary form

E22.d: Hypersecretion of anterior pituitary hormones, usually due to a GH-, prolactin- or ACTH-producing adenoma.
s: Acromegaly with enlargement of the extremities

E23.n: Hypofunction and other disorders of pituitary gland
E23.d: Deficiency of one or more pituitary hormones, including hypopituitarism and central diabetes insipidus.
s: Fatigue and hypotension due to ACTH deficiency
Hypogonadism with amenorrhea or erectile dysfunction
Polyuria with dilute urine in diabetes insipidus
Short stature in children due to GH deficiency

E24.d: Manifestations of chronic glucocorticoid excess, endogenous or exogenous, with Cushing disease being the ACTH-dependent pituitary form.

E25.d: Excess adrenal androgens, typically due to congenital adrenal hyperplasia with 21-hydroxylase deficiency.

E26.d: Autonomous aldosterone production, most commonly due to an adenoma or bilateral adrenal hyperplasia.

E27.d: Other adrenal disorders, including primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) and adrenal crisis.

E28.d: Ovarian dysfunctions, notably polycystic ovary syndrome and premature ovarian failure.

E29.d: Altered testicular function with insufficient or excessive androgen production and impaired spermatogenesis.

E30.n: Disorders of puberty, not elsewhere classified
E30.d: Disorders of the timing of puberty, including precocious puberty and delayed puberty.
s: Thelarche or testicular enlargement before the expected age
Growth acceleration and advanced bone age
Absence of sexual characteristics at the expected age

E31.d: Simultaneous involvement of several endocrine glands, such as the autoimmune polyglandular syndromes and multiple endocrine neoplasias.
s: Combination of adrenal insufficiency and autoimmune thyroid disease
Type 1 diabetes associated with other autoimmune conditions
Mucocutaneous candidiasis and hypoparathyroidism in type 1

E32.d: Diseases of the thymus, such as thymic hyperplasia, thymoma and thymic atrophy.
s: Association with myasthenia gravis in thymoma

E34.d: Residual category of miscellaneous endocrine disorders, including carcinoid syndrome and unclassified forms of short stature.
s: Facial flushing and diarrhea in carcinoid syndrome

E35.n: Disorders of endocrine glands in diseases classified elsewhere
E35.d: Code for glandular involvement secondary to diseases classified in other chapters, such as adrenal tuberculosis.

E40.d: Severe protein-energy malnutrition with a predominantly protein deficit, presenting with edema and hypoalbuminemia.
s: Edema of the limbs and face

E41.d: Severe malnutrition due to overall energy deficit, with marked wasting of muscle mass and fat, without edema.

E42.d: Mixed form of severe malnutrition, with the marked wasting of marasmus combined with the edema of kwashiorkor.

E43.d: Severe protein-energy malnutrition without characterization of the specific clinical form.
s: Weight far below that expected for age

E44.n: Protein-energy malnutrition of moderate and mild degree
E44.d: Protein-energy nutritional deficit of mild to moderate intensity, usually identified by anthropometry.

E45.d: Effects of a deficient nutritional state on growth and development, including nutritional dwarfism.

E46.d: Protein-energy malnutrition without specification of degree or clinical form.

E50.d: Hypovitaminosis A, the leading preventable cause of childhood blindness worldwide, with ocular and immune involvement.

E51.d: Vitamin B1 deficiency, causing beriberi and Wernicke encephalopathy, classically associated with chronic alcoholism.
s: High-output heart failure in wet beriberi
Amnesia and confabulation in Korsakoff syndrome

E52.d: Niacin deficiency leading to pellagra, classic in maize-dependent diets.

E53.n: Deficiency of other B group vitamins
E53.d: Deficiencies of other B-complex vitamins, such as pyridoxine, riboflavin and cobalamin.
s: Subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord
Seizures due to pyridoxine deficiency in infants

E54.d: Vitamin C deficiency, causing scurvy through failure of collagen synthesis.

E55.d: Vitamin D deficiency with impaired bone mineralization, causing rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.
s: Varus deformity of the lower limbs
Craniotabes and delayed closure of the fontanelles
Diffuse bone pain and muscle weakness

E56.d: Deficiencies of other vitamins, notably vitamin K and vitamin E.
s: Ataxia and neuropathy in vitamin E deficiency

E58.d: Insufficient dietary calcium intake, with effects on bone mass.

E59.d: Dietary selenium deficiency, associated with Keshan disease in endemic areas with soil poor in the element.

E60.d: Dietary zinc deficiency, with effects on skin, immunity and growth.
s: Growth retardation and poor wound healing

Urine with a maple syrup odor

Jaundice, cataract and sepsis in galactosemia
Clinical worsening after ingestion of the sugar involved

s: Pancreatitis when triglycerides are very high

E79.n: Disorders of purine and pyrimidine metabolism
E79.d: Errors of purine and pyrimidine metabolism, including hyperuricemia and Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.

E80.d: Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism, such as the porphyrias and Gilbert syndrome.

Urine that darkens on exposure to light
Cutaneous photosensitivity in the cutaneous porphyrias
Indirect hyperbilirubinemia on fasting in Gilbert syndrome

Elevated ferritin and transferrin saturation in hemochromatosis

s: Elevated chloride on the sweat test

s: Dry mucous membranes and reduced skin turgor

Arrhythmias in sodium and potassium disorders
Blood gases with altered pH and bicarbonate

E90.n: Nutritional and metabolic disorders in diseases classified elsewhere
E90.d: Code for nutritional and metabolic manifestations secondary to diseases classified in other chapters.

s: Motor signs of the underlying disease

F06.d: Psychotic, affective, anxiety or mild cognitive disorders caused directly by brain or systemic disease.

F07.d: Persistent change in personality or behavior after brain injury, encephalitis or head trauma.

F09.d: Mental disorder attributed to an organic or symptomatic cause without specification of the presentation; records cases in which the type of syndrome has not been defined.

Mydriasis, yawning and piloerection in withdrawal
Muscle pain and diarrhea in withdrawal

F12.d: Disorders due to use of marijuana and its derivatives, with intoxication, dependence and induced psychotic states.

F13.n: Mental and behavioural disorders due to use of sedatives or hypnotics
F13.d: Disorders due to use of benzodiazepines and other sedatives, with risk of dependence and severe withdrawal.

F14.n: Mental and behavioural disorders due to use of cocaine

F15.d: Disorders due to use of amphetamines, methamphetamine, caffeine and other stimulants, with intoxication and dependence.

F16.d: Disorders due to use of LSD, psilocybin and other hallucinogens, with perceptual alteration and possible psychotic reactions.

F17.n: Mental and behavioural disorders due to use of tobacco
F17.d: Disorders due to tobacco use, mainly nicotine dependence and its withdrawal syndrome.

F18.n: Mental and behavioural disorders due to use of volatile solvents
F18.d: Disorders due to use of inhalants such as glue, paint thinner and lança-perfume, with intoxication and neurological damage.

F19.n: Mental and behavioural disorders due to multiple drug use and use of other psychoactive substances
F19.d: Disorders due to use of several psychoactive substances without predominance of any one, or of substances not listed.

Preserved functioning outside the delusional theme

s: Delusion identical to that of the inducer

F25.d: Presentation with prominent schizophrenic and affective (manic or depressive) symptoms in the same episode.

F29.d: Psychosis without an identified organic cause whose type has not been specified, used when information is insufficient.

s: Pressured speech and flight of ideas

F39.d: Affective disorder without specification of type, used when there are no data to classify it.

s: Anxiety when the ritual is prevented

s: Paralysis or anesthesia without a lesion

F45.d: Multiple, persistent physical symptoms without sufficient organic explanation, with repeated seeking of medical care.

F52.n: Sexual dysfunction, not caused by organic disorder or disease

F53.d: Mental disorders beginning within six weeks after childbirth that do not meet the criteria for other categories.

F60.d: Persistent and inflexible personality patterns, such as borderline, antisocial or paranoid, that cause distress or impairment.
s: Onset in adolescence or young adulthood

F61.d: Traits of several personality disorders without predominance of one type, causing impairment.
s: Traits of more than one personality type

F62.n: Enduring personality changes, not attributable to brain damage and disease
F62.d: Persistent personality change after a catastrophic experience or severe psychiatric illness, without brain injury.

s: Desire for social or medical transition

s: Recurrent atypical sexual fantasies or urges

F66.n: Psychological and behavioural disorders associated with sexual development and orientation
F66.d: Psychological distress related to sexual development or orientation, such as sexual maturation disorder; orientation itself is not a disorder.

F68.n: Other disorders of adult personality and behaviour

F69.n: Unspecified disorder of adult personality and behaviour

s: Need for support in complex decisions

F71.d: Intellectual disability with an IQ of approximately 35 to 49, with marked developmental delay and need for continuous support.

F72.d: Intellectual disability with an IQ of approximately 20 to 34, with major limitation of language and independence.

F73.d: Intellectual disability with an IQ below 20, with total dependence and frequently associated with severe neurological deficits.

F78.d: Intellectual disability whose degree is difficult to assess because of associated sensory or physical deficits.

F79.d: Evident intellectual disability without sufficient information to define its degree.

F80.n: Specific developmental disorders of speech and language
F80.d: Delay or disturbance in the acquisition of speech and language without intellectual, sensory or neurological impairment to explain it.

F81.n: Specific developmental disorders of scholastic skills
F81.d: Specific difficulty in reading, writing or mathematics, disproportionate to intelligence and schooling, such as dyslexia.

F82.n: Specific developmental disorder of motor function
F82.d: Delay in motor coordination without an evident neurological cause, impairing daily and school activities.

F83.d: Combination of specific disorders of speech, learning and motor function without predominance of any one of them.

F84.d: Neurodevelopmental disorders with deficits in social interaction and communication and restricted, repetitive behaviors, such as autism.

F88.d: Other disorders of psychological development not classified in the specific categories, such as developmental agnosia.

F89.d: Disorder of psychological development without specification of type.

F90.d: Persistent pattern of inattention, hyperactivity and impulsivity beginning in childhood, causing impairment in several settings.

F91.d: Repetitive pattern of behavior that violates rules and the rights of others, such as aggression, destruction and lying.

F92.n: Mixed disorders of conduct and emotions
F92.d: Combination of conduct disorder with marked emotional symptoms, such as depression or anxiety.

F93.n: Emotional disorders with onset specific to childhood
F93.d: Emotional disorders typical of childhood, such as separation anxiety, phobias and sibling rivalry.

F94.n: Disorders of social functioning with onset specific to childhood and adolescence

s: Abnormal CSF without an identified agent

G07.d: Intracranial or intraspinal abscess or granuloma resulting from a disease classified in another chapter, such as tuberculosis or neurocysticercosis.

Vascular parkinsonism predominantly in the lower limbs

Urge to move the legs at rest

Aphasia and apraxia in intermediate stages

Focal neurological relapses with partial recovery

Risk of neuronal injury and hyperthermia

Tongue deviation with hypoglossal nerve lesion

Ramsay Hunt syndrome with auricular vesicles

Paresthesia in the first three fingers

Meralgia paresthetica on the lateral aspect of the thigh

G64.n: Other disorders of peripheral nervous system

Bulbar weakness with dysphagia and dysarthria

G71.d: Primary muscle diseases of genetic basis, including muscular dystrophies, myotonias and congenital myopathies.

s: Episodic weakness associated with a potassium disorder

Proximal weakness with increment after exercise

Spasticity and hyperreflexia in the chronic phase

s: Horner syndrome in ocular sympathetic lesions

Myelopathy with spasticity and sensory level

Point of pus at the margin

Reflux of discharge on pressure over the lacrimal sac

Reduced vision if the macula is involved

H59.d: Eye complications after procedures, such as bullous keratopathy after cataract surgery and vitreous syndrome, not classified elsewhere.

Edema and erythema of the canal

s: Pain and swelling of the pinna in perichondritis

s: Opaque tympanic membrane with fluid level

H66.d: Acute or chronic infection of the middle ear with purulent discharge, common in children.

H67.n: Otitis media in diseases classified elsewhere
H67.d: Otitis media secondary to diseases from other chapters, such as measles, influenza or tuberculosis; the presentation depends on the underlying disease.

s: Improvement when lying down in patulous tube

s: Opacification of the mastoid on CT

H71.d: Accumulation of keratinized squamous epithelium in the middle ear, which grows and erodes bony structures.
s: Whitish mass in the middle ear

H72.d: Loss of continuity of the tympanic membrane due to infection, trauma or barotrauma.

H73.d: Other changes in the eardrum, such as myringitis and atrophy or retraction of the membrane.

H74.n: Other disorders of middle ear and mastoid
H74.d: Other disorders of the middle ear and mastoid, such as tympanosclerosis, ossicular discontinuity and polyp.

H75.n: Other disorders of middle ear and mastoid in diseases classified elsewhere
H75.d: Changes in the middle ear and mastoid secondary to diseases classified elsewhere, such as tuberculosis; the presentation depends on the underlying disease.

H81.d: Disorders of the labyrinth and vestibular nerve, such as Ménière disease, BPPV and vestibular neuritis.
s: Fluctuating hearing loss and tinnitus in Ménière disease
Vertigo on changing head position in BPPV

H82.n: Vertiginous syndromes in diseases classified elsewhere
H82.d: Vertigo secondary to diseases classified elsewhere; the presentation depends on the underlying disease.

s: Audiometric notch at 4 kHz in noise-induced loss

H90.d: Hearing loss of conductive, sensorineural or mixed type, unilateral or bilateral, confirmed by audiometry.
s: Air-bone gap in the conductive form

s: Bilateral symmetric high-frequency loss in presbycusis

H95.n: Postprocedural disorders of ear and mastoid process, not elsewhere classified
H95.d: Complications after ear and mastoid surgery, such as a mastoidectomy cavity with chronic inflammation.
s: Persistent otorrhea in the operated cavity

I00.n: Rheumatic fever without mention of heart involvement

s: Raised ASO titer and high ESR

s: Cardiomegaly and signs of heart failure

I02.d: Late neurological manifestation of rheumatic fever, due to involvement of the basal ganglia.

s: Atrial fibrillation and enlarged left atrium

I06.d: Chronic rheumatic involvement of the aortic valve, presenting with stenosis, regurgitation or a mixed lesion.
s: Ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids
Blowing diastolic murmur in the aortic area
Bounding pulse or pulsus parvus et tardus

s: Jugular venous distension with prominent v wave

s: Murmurs in more than one area

I09.d: Residual category for rheumatic cardiac manifestations not classified under the specific headings.

I13.d: Simultaneous cardiac and renal target-organ damage attributed to chronic arterial hypertension.

I15.d: Arterial hypertension with an identifiable underlying cause, renal, endocrine or vascular.
s: Hypertension resistant to multiple drug classes
Abdominal bruit in renal artery stenosis

I20.d: Transient myocardial ischemia due to an imbalance between supply and demand, without cell necrosis.
s: Radiation to the left arm or jaw

I21.d: Myocardial necrosis due to acute coronary occlusion, usually from rupture of an atherosclerotic plaque.

Dyspnea and a sense of impending doom

New ST changes on the ECG

Acute mitral regurgitation due to papillary muscle rupture
Tamponade due to free wall rupture

I24.d: Acute ischemic syndromes that do not meet the criteria for established infarction.
s: Transient ischemic changes on the ECG

I25.d: Established coronary atherosclerosis with chronic ischemia and progressive myocardial dysfunction.

I27.d: Pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale resulting from chronic lung or vascular diseases.

Jugular venous distension and limb edema

I28.d: Various disorders of the pulmonary vessels, including arteriovenous fistulas and aneurysms.
s: Continuous murmur over a lung field

s: Jugular venous distension with Kussmaul sign

I32.d: Pericardial involvement secondary to systemic, infectious or neoplastic diseases classified elsewhere.

I33.d: Infection of the valvular endocardium, with formation of vegetations and risk of systemic embolization.
s: Fever with a new heart murmur

I34.d: Mitral dysfunction of degenerative, ischemic or myxomatous cause, without rheumatic origin.
s: Holosystolic murmur radiating to the axilla

I35.d: Non-rheumatic aortic disease, most often degenerative calcific stenosis of the elderly.
s: Harsh systolic murmur in the aortic area

I36.d: Non-rheumatic tricuspid dysfunction, predominantly functional regurgitation due to annular dilatation.
s: Systolic murmur that increases on inspiration
Jugular venous distension with v wave

I37.d: Stenosis or regurgitation of the pulmonary valve, of congenital etiology in most cases.
s: Ejection systolic murmur in the pulmonary area

I38.d: Documented endocarditis without identification of the affected valve in the clinical record.

I39.n: Endocarditis and heart valve disorders in diseases classified elsewhere
I39.d: Endocardial or valvular involvement as a manifestation of a systemic disease classified under another heading.
s: Heart murmur in the setting of systemic disease

I40.d: Acute inflammation of the myocardium, often post-viral, with ventricular dysfunction and a risk of arrhythmias.
s: Chest pain after a viral illness

I41.d: Myocarditis as a manifestation of an infectious or systemic disease classified elsewhere.
s: Ventricular dysfunction during the course of the underlying disease

I42.d: Primary diseases of the heart muscle, with dilated, hypertrophic or restrictive phenotypes.
s: Murmur that increases with Valsalva in the hypertrophic form

I43.d: Myocardial involvement secondary to metabolic, infiltrative or systemic diseases classified elsewhere.
s: Heart failure in the setting of systemic disease

s: Wide QRS with rSR pattern in V1
Delta wave and short PR in pre-excitation

s: Ventricular fibrillation or asystole on the monitor

I47.d: Tachyarrhythmias with abrupt onset and termination, of supraventricular or ventricular origin.
s: Palpitations with sudden onset and offset
Narrow or wide QRS depending on the origin

I48.d: Supraventricular arrhythmia with disorganized atrial activation, loss of effective atrial contraction and embolic risk.
s: Absent P waves with variable RR

I49.d: Other heart rhythm abnormalities, including extrasystoles and sinus node dysfunction.
s: Symptomatic bradycardia in sinus node disease

I50.d: Clinical syndrome in which the heart does not maintain an output adequate to tissue demands.
s: Lower limb edema and jugular venous distension

s: Progressive decline in level of consciousness

Atrial fibrillation as an embolic source

Diastolic murmur due to aortic regurgitation

I77.n: Other disorders of arteries and arterioles

I79.n: Disorders of arteries, arterioles and capillaries in diseases classified elsewhere
I79.d: Arterial and capillary changes as a manifestation of systemic diseases classified elsewhere.

Ochre dermatitis and medial malleolar ulcer

s: Venous ulcer in the malleolar region

Blood pressure drop on postural testing

I98.d: Circulatory manifestations attributed to systemic diseases classified in other chapters.

Fissures at the corners of the mouth

M95.d: Acquired deformities of the musculoskeletal system, such as deformities of the nose, ear, chest, and pelvis.

M96.n: Postprocedural musculoskeletal disorders, not elsewhere classified
M96.d: Musculoskeletal complications after procedures, such as pseudarthrosis after arthrodesis, postlaminectomy syndrome, and postirradiation osteopathy.

M99.d: Segmental and biomechanical dysfunctions of the spine and other regions, used mainly in manipulation and rehabilitation.

N00.d: Acute glomerular inflammation with hematuria, proteinuria, and salt and water retention, classically post-streptococcal.
s: Red blood cell casts in the sediment

N01.d: Glomerulonephritis with loss of kidney function over days to weeks, corresponding to crescentic glomerulonephritis.
s: Hematuria with red blood cell casts

N02.d: Repeated or continuous glomerular hematuria, with IgA nephropathy as the most frequent cause.

N03.d: Glomerular injury with a protracted course, with hematuria, proteinuria, and slow decline in kidney function.
