N04.d: Glomerular injury with massive proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, edema, and dyslipidemia, due to loss of the filtration barrier.

N05.d: Glomerular syndrome without a defined histological pattern or course; category used when characterization is lacking.

N06.n: Isolated proteinuria with specified morphological lesion
N06.d: Proteinuria without hematuria or loss of function, with a glomerular lesion defined by biopsy.

N07.d: Glomerular diseases of genetic origin, with Alport syndrome as the classic prototype.

N08.n: Glomerular disorders in diseases classified elsewhere
N08.d: Glomerular involvement secondary to systemic disease, such as lupus, diabetes, amyloidosis, or vasculitides.
s: Proteinuria in the setting of systemic disease
Extrarenal manifestations of the underlying disease

N10.d: Acute inflammation of the renal interstitium and tubules, often due to drug hypersensitivity or infection.

N11.d: Chronic tubulointerstitial injury, including reflux nephropathy and chronic pyelonephritis with renal scarring.

N12.n: Tubulo-interstitial nephritis, not specified as acute or chronic
N12.d: Tubulointerstitial nephritis without an acute or chronic course defined in the diagnostic record.

N13.d: Renal impairment due to obstruction of urine flow or to vesicoureteral reflux, with hydronephrosis.

N14.n: Drug- and heavy-metal-induced tubulo-interstitial and tubular conditions
N14.d: Tubular and interstitial injury due to nephrotoxins, such as analgesics, iodinated contrast, chemotherapeutic agents, and heavy metals.
s: Polyuria due to a concentrating defect

N15.d: Residual group of tubulointerstitial diseases, including perinephric abscess and Balkan nephropathy.

N16.n: Renal tubulo-interstitial disorders in diseases classified elsewhere
N16.d: Tubulointerstitial involvement secondary to systemic diseases, such as myeloma, sarcoidosis, or leukemias.

N17.d: Abrupt fall in glomerular filtration over hours to days, with retention of nitrogenous waste products.
s: Rapid rise in creatinine and urea

N18.d: Progressive and irreversible loss of kidney function for more than three months, staged by glomerular filtration rate.

N19.d: Uremia without characterization of an acute or chronic course at the time of recording.

N20.d: Stones in the kidney or ureter, with risk of urinary flow obstruction and renal colic.
s: Flank colic radiating to the groin
Restlessness with no position of relief

N21.d: Stones in the bladder or urethra, often associated with bladder outlet obstruction or an indwelling catheter.

N22.n: Calculus of urinary tract in diseases classified elsewhere
N22.d: Lower urinary tract lithiasis secondary to systemic diseases, such as schistosomiasis.

N23.d: Acute colicky low back pain attributed to ureteral obstruction, without a confirmed stone.
s: Radiation to the flank and genitalia

N25.n: Disorders resulting from impaired renal tubular function
N25.d: Disorders of tubular handling of water, electrolytes, and acid-base balance, including nephrogenic diabetes insipidus and renal osteodystrophy.

N26.d: Kidney reduced in size due to diffuse atrophy, a finding of advanced chronic kidney disease of undetermined cause.

N27.d: Congenital reduction of renal mass, unilateral or bilateral, without a defined etiology.

N28.n: Other disorders of kidney and ureter, not elsewhere classified
N28.d: Residual category for miscellaneous renal and ureteral conditions, such as ischemia, infarction, and acquired renal cysts.

N29.n: Other disorders of kidney and ureter in diseases classified elsewhere
N29.d: Renal and ureteral changes secondary to diseases classified in other chapters, such as schistosomiasis and syphilis.

N30.d: Inflammation of the bladder, usually bacterial infection, but also radiation-induced, chemical, or interstitial.
s: Absence of fever in uncomplicated forms

N31.n: Neuromuscular dysfunction of bladder, not elsewhere classified
N31.d: Bladder dysfunction due to neurological injury, impairing storage or emptying (neurogenic bladder).
s: Urinary retention or elevated post-void residual

N32.d: Group of miscellaneous bladder conditions, including diverticulum, vesical fistula, bladder neck obstruction and calcification.

N33.n: Bladder disorders in diseases classified elsewhere
N33.d: Bladder involvement secondary to diseases from other chapters, such as schistosomiasis and tuberculosis.

N34.d: Urethral inflammation, classically due to gonococcus or chlamydia, or urethral symptoms without an identified uropathogen.

N35.d: Scarring narrowing of the urethra, usually post-traumatic, post-infectious or due to instrumentation.

N36.d: Various urethral conditions, such as fistula, diverticulum and urethral caruncle.

N37.n: Urethral disorders in diseases classified elsewhere
N37.d: Urethral changes secondary to diseases classified in other chapters.

N39.d: Residual category of the urinary tract, covering urinary tract infection of unspecified site and urinary incontinence.

N40.d: Benign growth of the prostatic transition zone, causing bladder outlet obstruction in older men.

N41.d: Acute or chronic prostatic inflammation, of bacterial or non-bacterial origin (chronic pelvic pain).
s: Fever and chills in the acute form
Tender prostate on digital rectal examination

N42.d: Other prostatic conditions, including calculus, atrophy, congestion and isolated PSA elevation.

N43.d: Fluid collection in the tunica vaginalis (hydrocele) or epididymal cyst containing spermatozoa (spermatocele).
s: Testis palpable separately from the cyst

N44.d: Rotation of the spermatic cord with testicular ischemia, a surgical emergency in adolescents.

N45.d: Inflammation of the testis and/or epididymis, due to ascending urogenital or viral infection, such as mumps.

N46.d: Inability to achieve pregnancy due to a male factor, with azoospermia or oligospermia on semen analysis.

N47.d: Preputial disorders: phimosis prevents retraction; paraphimosis is a retracted foreskin that constricts the glans.
s: Constricting ring with glans edema in paraphimosis

N48.d: Various penile conditions, including Peyronie disease, priapism, balanoposthitis and organic erectile dysfunction.

N49.n: Inflammatory disorders of male genital organs, not elsewhere classified
N49.d: Inflammation of male genital structures such as the seminal vesicle, spermatic cord and scrotum, including Fournier gangrene.
s: Erythema and crepitus in necrotizing fasciitis

N50.n: Other disorders of male genital organs
N50.d: Residual group of male genital disorders, such as testicular atrophy, varicocele and chronic scrotal pain.

N51.n: Disorders of male genital organs in diseases classified elsewhere
N51.d: Male genital involvement secondary to diseases from other chapters, such as tuberculosis and herpes.

N60.d: Benign breast changes, including fibrocystic change, solitary cyst and duct ectasia.
s: Cysts with anechoic content on ultrasound

N61.d: Inflammation of the breast, including puerperal mastitis and breast abscess, usually due to Staphylococcus aureus.
s: History of nipple fissure and breastfeeding

N62.d: Excessive increase in breast volume, including female gigantomastia and male gynecomastia.
s: Palpable retroareolar glandular tissue in gynecomastia
Neck and shoulder pain due to weight

N63.d: Palpable or imaging-detected breast lump without defined histological characterization; requires investigation.
s: Incidental finding on mammography or ultrasound

N64.d: Various breast conditions, including galactorrhea not associated with childbirth, nipple fissure, nipple retraction and atrophy.

N70.d: Inflammation of the fallopian tubes and ovaries, the main component of ascending pelvic inflammatory disease.

N71.n: Inflammatory disease of uterus, except cervix
N71.d: Inflammation of the uterine body (endometritis and myometritis), often postpartum, post-abortion or post-instrumentation.

N72.d: Cervicitis, inflammation of the uterine cervix, commonly due to chlamydia or gonococcus.

N73.d: Other female pelvic infections, including parametritis, pelvic cellulitis and pelvic peritonitis.

N74.n: Female pelvic inflammatory disorders in diseases classified elsewhere
N74.d: Female pelvic inflammation secondary to diseases classified in other chapters, such as tuberculosis and chlamydia.

N75.d: Conditions of the greater vestibular gland: cyst due to duct obstruction, or abscess when infected.
s: Unilateral mass in the posterior vulva
Severe pain and fluctuance in abscess

N76.n: Other inflammation of vagina and vulva
N76.d: Inflammation of the vagina and vulva, including bacterial vaginosis, candidiasis and atrophic vulvovaginitis.

N77.n: Vulvovaginal ulceration and inflammation in diseases classified elsewhere
N77.d: Inflammatory or ulcerative vulvovaginal lesions secondary to diseases from other chapters, such as herpes and Behçet disease.

N80.d: Functioning endometrial tissue outside the uterine cavity, causing inflammation, pain and pelvic adhesions.

N81.d: Descent of the pelvic organs through the vaginal canal due to pelvic floor failure, including cystocele and rectocele.
s: Sensation of a bulge or vaginal heaviness

N82.d: Abnormal communications between the genital tract and neighboring organs, such as vesicovaginal or rectovaginal fistula.
s: Continuous leakage of urine through the vagina
Passage of feces or gas through the vagina
History of obstructed labor or pelvic surgery

N83.n: Noninflammatory disorders of ovary, fallopian tube and broad ligament
N83.d: Noninflammatory adnexal disorders, including follicular cysts, corpus luteum cyst and polycystic ovary syndrome.
s: Acute pelvic pain on rupture or torsion

N84.d: Polypoid growths of the female genital tract, most frequent in the endometrium and the cervix.

N85.n: Other noninflammatory disorders of uterus, except cervix
N85.d: Noninflammatory uterine disorders, including endometrial hyperplasia, adenomyosis and intrauterine synechiae.
s: Dysmenorrhea and globular uterus in adenomyosis

N86.n: Erosion and ectropion of cervix uteri
N86.d: Exposure of the endocervical columnar epithelium on the ectocervix, a common and usually physiological finding.
s: Erythematous area around the external os

N87.d: Dysplastic changes of the cervical epithelium (CIN), HPV-associated precursor lesions of cervical cancer.

N88.n: Other noninflammatory disorders of cervix uteri
N88.d: Other noninflammatory cervical changes, such as stenosis and cervical incompetence.
s: Painless cervical dilation in the second trimester

N89.d: Noninflammatory vaginal disorders, including vaginal dysplasia, stenosis and non-infectious leukorrhea.
s: Vaginal discharge without an identified agent

N90.n: Other noninflammatory disorders of vulva and perineum
N90.d: Noninflammatory vulvar and perineal changes, such as lichen sclerosus, dystrophies and vulvar dysplasia.

N91.d: Absence or reduction of menstrual flow: primary amenorrhea, secondary amenorrhea and oligomenorrhea.
s: No menarche by the expected age
Absence of menstruation for three cycles
Cycles with intervals longer than 35 days

N92.d: Changes in the menstrual pattern due to excessive volume, frequency or irregularity of cycles.
s: Cycles with intervals shorter than 21 days

N93.n: Other abnormal uterine and vaginal bleeding
N93.d: Genital bleeding outside the menstrual pattern, including postcoital bleeding and dysfunctional uterine bleeding.
s: Anovulatory bleeding without a structural cause

N94.n: Pain and other conditions associated with female genital organs and menstrual cycle
N94.d: Pain and symptoms related to the female genital organs and the cycle, such as dysmenorrhea, mittelschmerz and premenstrual tension.
s: Menstrual cramps in the lower abdomen

N95.d: Manifestations of climacteric hypoestrogenism, with vasomotor symptoms and genitourinary atrophy.

N96.d: Consecutive, repeated spontaneous pregnancy losses, prompting investigation of a maternal or embryonic cause.

N97.d: Absence of pregnancy after one year of trying, due to ovulatory, tubal or uterine factors.

N98.d: Complications of assisted reproductive techniques, notably ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome.

N99.n: Postprocedural disorders of genitourinary system, not elsewhere classified
N99.d: Genitourinary changes resulting from procedures, such as adhesions, strictures and dysfunction after surgery.

O00.d: Implantation of the embryo outside the uterine cavity, mainly in the fallopian tube, with risk of rupture and internal hemorrhage.
s: Positive beta-hCG without an intrauterine gestational sac

O01.d: Abnormal proliferation of the trophoblast with hydropic villi, complete or partial, with risk of trophoblastic neoplasia.
s: Vaginal bleeding in the first trimester

O02.d: Abnormal products of conception, such as blighted ovum (anembryonic pregnancy), missed abortion and non-hydatidiform mole.

O03.d: Spontaneous pregnancy loss before 20–22 weeks, frequently due to chromosomal abnormalities.
s: Open or closed cervix depending on the stage

O04.d: Termination of pregnancy performed within the circumstances provided for by law or on medical indication.
s: Risk of retained products of conception

O05.d: Other types of abortion not classified as spontaneous or legal, recorded according to the associated complication.

O06.d: Abortion without specification of type, recorded according to the presence or absence of complications.

O07.d: Unsuccessful attempt to terminate pregnancy, with persistence of the pregnancy or complications.

O08.n: Complications following abortion and ectopic and molar pregnancy
O08.d: Complications after abortion or ectopic or molar pregnancy, such as infection, hemorrhage, embolism and injury to pelvic organs.

O10.n: Pre-existing hypertension complicating pregnancy, childbirth and the puerperium
O10.d: Arterial hypertension diagnosed before pregnancy or before 20 weeks, persisting into the puerperium.
s: BP of 140/90 or higher before 20 weeks

O11.n: Pre-existing hypertensive disorder with superimposed proteinuria
O11.d: Chronic hypertension with new-onset proteinuria or target-organ damage after 20 weeks of gestation.

O12.n: Gestational [pregnancy-induced] oedema and proteinuria without hypertension
O12.d: Edema and/or proteinuria arising during pregnancy without elevated blood pressure.

O13.d: Elevated blood pressure after 20 weeks without proteinuria or target-organ damage, resolving in the puerperium.
s: BP of 140/90 or higher after 20 weeks

O14.d: Pre-eclampsia: hypertension after 20 weeks with proteinuria or target-organ dysfunction due to placental and endothelial dysfunction.

O15.d: Tonic-clonic seizures in a pregnant or postpartum woman with pre-eclampsia, with no other neurological cause.

O16.d: Maternal hypertension without classification of type, used when clinical information is insufficient.

O20.d: Vaginal bleeding before 20 weeks, including threatened abortion, with a still viable pregnancy.

O21.d: Persistent nausea and vomiting in pregnancy; in the severe form (hyperemesis gravidarum) with dehydration and metabolic disturbances.

O22.d: Venous complications in pregnancy, such as varicose veins, hemorrhoids, and deep and superficial venous thrombosis.
s: Varicose veins of the legs or vulva

O23.n: Infections of genitourinary tract in pregnancy
O23.d: Urinary and genital infections during pregnancy, including bacteriuria, cystitis and pyelonephritis.

O24.d: Pre-existing diabetes or diabetes diagnosed in pregnancy (gestational), due to insulin resistance induced by placental hormones.
s: Hyperglycemia on the oral glucose tolerance test
Fasting glucose between 92 and 125 in gestational diabetes

O25.d: Deficient nutritional status in pregnancy, with insufficient weight gain and risk to the fetus.

O26.n: Maternal care for other conditions predominantly related to pregnancy
O26.d: Pregnancy-related complications, such as excessive weight gain, intrahepatic cholestasis, herpes gestationis and symphysis subluxation.

O28.n: Abnormal findings on antenatal screening of mother
O28.d: Abnormal findings on prenatal screening tests without a defined diagnosis, such as biochemical, ultrasonographic or cytogenetic abnormalities.

O29.d: Complications of anesthesia administered during pregnancy, such as aspiration, reactions to the anesthetic and failed intubation.

O30.d: Pregnancy with two or more fetuses, twin or higher order, with increased risk of maternal and fetal complications.
s: More than one fetus on ultrasound

O31.d: Complications specific to multiple pregnancy, such as death of one fetus, fetus papyraceus and twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome.
s: Polyhydramnios in one sac and oligohydramnios in the other

O32.n: Maternal care for known or suspected malpresentation of fetus
O32.d: Care of the pregnant woman for abnormal fetal presentation, such as breech, transverse or face, with implications for the mode of delivery.
s: Fetal heart sounds in an atypical location
Planning of cesarean section or version

O33.n: Maternal care for known or suspected disproportion
O33.d: Care of the pregnant woman for known or suspected disproportion between the fetus and the maternal pelvis.

O34.n: Maternal care for known or suspected abnormality of pelvic organs
O34.d: Care of the pregnant woman for abnormalities of the uterus, cervix or other pelvic organs, such as a previous uterine scar and cervical incompetence.

O35.n: Maternal care for known or suspected fetal abnormality and damage
O35.d: Care of the pregnant woman for known or suspected fetal abnormality or damage, such as CNS malformations and chromosomal abnormalities.
s: Exposure to infection or a teratogenic drug

O36.n: Maternal care for other known or suspected fetal problems
O36.d: Care of the pregnant woman for other fetal problems, such as isoimmunization, growth restriction, macrosomia and fetal death.

O40.d: Increased amniotic fluid volume, idiopathic or associated with diabetes, malformations or fetal infections.

O41.n: Other disorders of amniotic fluid and membranes
O41.d: Disorders of the membranes and amniotic fluid, such as oligohydramnios and chorioamnionitis.

O42.d: Rupture of the amniotic membranes before the onset of labor, at term or preterm.
s: Leakage of fluid from the vagina
Fluid pooling in the posterior fornix

O43.d: Placental abnormalities, such as placenta accreta spectrum, placental transfusion syndromes and placental insufficiency.

O44.d: Implantation of the placenta over or near the internal cervical os.
s: Painless vaginal bleeding in the 3rd trimester

O45.d: Separation of a normally implanted placenta before birth, usually associated with hypertension.

O46.d: Antepartum hemorrhage without a cause classified elsewhere, including cases with coagulation defect.

O47.d: Uterine contractions without progressive cervical change.

O48.d: Pregnancy exceeding 42 completed weeks, with risk of placental insufficiency and macrosomia.
s: Gestational age of 42 weeks or more

O60.d: Onset of regular contractions with cervical change before 37 weeks of gestation.

O61.d: Absence of effective labor after an attempt at pharmacological or mechanical induction.

O62.d: Ineffective or excessive uterine contractions, such as uterine inertia, tachysystole and hypertonia.

O63.d: Labor of excessive duration, in the first or second stage.

O64.n: Obstructed labour due to malposition and malpresentation of fetus
O64.d: Arrest of progress due to abnormal fetal position or presentation, such as persistent occipitoposterior position and shoulder presentation.

O65.n: Obstructed labour due to maternal pelvic abnormality
O65.d: Arrest of progress due to abnormalities of the maternal pelvis, such as a narrow or deformed pelvis.

O66.d: Obstructed labor from other causes, such as shoulder dystocia and a very large fetus.

O67.n: Labour and delivery complicated by intrapartum haemorrhage, not elsewhere classified
O67.d: Bleeding during labor not attributable to abruption or placenta previa, including that due to coagulopathy.

O68.n: Labour and delivery complicated by fetal stress [distress]
O68.d: Labor with signs of fetal compromise, such as fetal heart rate abnormalities or meconium.

O69.n: Labour and delivery complicated by umbilical cord complications
O69.d: Umbilical cord complications at delivery, such as prolapse, tight nuchal cord and true knot.

O70.d: Perineal laceration during delivery, graded from 1st to 4th degree according to involvement of muscles and the anal sphincter.

O71.d: Obstetric trauma such as uterine rupture, cervical and vaginal lacerations, uterine inversion and pelvic hematoma.

O72.d: Excessive blood loss after delivery, mainly due to uterine atony, retained placenta or lacerations.
s: Bleeding greater than 500 mL in vaginal delivery

O73.n: Retained placenta and membranes, without haemorrhage
O73.d: Retention of the placenta or membranes after delivery, without hemorrhage at the time.

O74.n: Complications of anaesthesia during labour and delivery
O74.d: Anesthetic complications during labor and delivery, such as aspiration, hypotension due to neuraxial block and post-dural puncture headache.

O75.n: Other complications of labour and delivery, not elsewhere classified
O75.d: Various complications of labor and delivery, such as obstetric shock, intrapartum fever and maternal distress.
s: Delivery after prolonged rupture of membranes

O80.d: Descriptive-purpose code for an uncomplicated single spontaneous vaginal delivery, used to record an uneventful birth.

O81.n: Single delivery by forceps and vacuum extractor
O81.d: Records a single vaginal delivery assisted by forceps or vacuum extractor, usually due to a prolonged second stage or fetal distress.

O82.d: Records a single delivery by cesarean section, elective or emergency.

O83.d: Records other assisted single deliveries, such as assisted breech delivery and obstetric maneuvers.

O84.d: Records the delivery of a multiple pregnancy, according to the mode of birth of each fetus.

O85.d: Infection of the genital tract after delivery, mainly endometritis, which may progress to sepsis.
s: Fever more than 24 hours after delivery

O86.d: Other puerperal infections, such as surgical wound infection, urinary infection and puerperal fever of unknown origin.

O87.d: Venous complications in the puerperium, such as deep vein thrombosis, superficial thrombophlebitis and hemorrhoids.

O88.d: Embolism in pregnancy or the puerperium, such as thrombotic pulmonary embolism, air embolism and amniotic fluid embolism.

O89.n: Complications of anaesthesia during the puerperium
O89.d: Complications of anesthesia in the puerperium, such as aspiration, anesthetic reactions and post-dural puncture headache.

O90.n: Complications of the puerperium, not elsewhere classified
O90.d: Various puerperal complications, such as wound dehiscence, peripartum cardiomyopathy and postpartum thyroiditis.

O91.n: Infections of breast associated with childbirth
O91.d: Breast infections related to childbirth and lactation, such as mastitis and breast abscess.

O92.n: Other disorders of breast and lactation associated with childbirth
O92.d: Breast and lactation disorders in the puerperium, such as nipple fissure, engorgement and hypogalactia.

O94.n: Sequelae of complication of pregnancy, childbirth and the puerperium
O94.d: Records late sequelae of complications of pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium, used to indicate the cause of residual conditions.

O95.d: Records maternal death from an unspecified obstetric cause during pregnancy, childbirth or the puerperium.

O96.n: Death from any obstetric cause occurring more than 42 days but less than one year after delivery
O96.d: Records late maternal death from an obstetric cause occurring between 42 days and 1 year after delivery.

O97.n: Death from sequelae of direct obstetric causes
O97.d: Records death from sequelae of direct obstetric causes occurring one year or more after delivery.

O98.n: Maternal infectious and parasitic diseases classifiable elsewhere but complicating pregnancy, childbirth and the puerperium
O98.d: Maternal infectious diseases from other chapters that complicate pregnancy, such as syphilis, tuberculosis, HIV and hepatitis; the clinical picture depends on the infection.

O99.n: Other maternal diseases classifiable elsewhere but complicating pregnancy, childbirth and the puerperium
O99.d: Maternal diseases from other chapters that complicate pregnancy, such as anemia, heart disease, respiratory and endocrine diseases; the clinical picture depends on the disease.

P00.n: Fetus and newborn affected by maternal conditions that may be unrelated to present pregnancy
P00.d: Records effects on the fetus or newborn of maternal diseases, such as hypertension, infections and kidney diseases, not necessarily related to the pregnancy.

P01.n: Fetus and newborn affected by maternal complications of pregnancy
P01.d: Records effects on the fetus or newborn of maternal complications of pregnancy, such as cervical incompetence, premature rupture of membranes and oligohydramnios.

P02.n: Fetus and newborn affected by complications of placenta, cord and membranes
P02.d: Records effects on the fetus or newborn of complications of the placenta, umbilical cord and membranes, such as placental abruption and cord prolapse.

P03.n: Fetus and newborn affected by other complications of labour and delivery
P03.d: Records effects on the fetus or newborn of complications of labor, such as malpresentation, instrumental delivery and cesarean section.

P04.n: Fetus and newborn affected by noxious influences transmitted via placenta or breast milk
P04.d: Effects on the fetus or newborn of substances transmitted via the placenta or breast milk, such as alcohol, tobacco, drugs and medications.

P05.n: Slow fetal growth and fetal malnutrition
P05.d: Fetal growth below that expected for gestational age, due to maternal, placental or fetal causes.

P07.n: Disorders related to short gestation and low birth weight, not elsewhere classified
P07.d: Birth before 37 weeks and/or low birth weight, with immaturity of organs and systems.

P08.n: Disorders related to long gestation and high birth weight
P08.d: Birth after 42 weeks or with high weight, with risk of birth trauma and metabolic disorders.
s: Weight above the 90th percentile or above 4,000 g

P10.n: Intracranial laceration and haemorrhage due to birth injury
P10.d: Intracranial hemorrhage due to mechanical trauma during delivery, such as subdural hematoma or subarachnoid hemorrhage.

P11.n: Other birth injuries to central nervous system
P11.d: Other traumatic CNS injuries during delivery, such as cerebral edema, spinal cord injury and facial palsy.

P12.d: Scalp injuries during delivery, such as caput succedaneum, cephalohematoma and subgaleal hematoma.

P13.d: Fractures during delivery, mainly of the clavicle, humerus and femur.

P14.n: Birth injury to peripheral nervous system
P14.d: Peripheral nerve injuries during delivery, mainly of the brachial plexus and phrenic nerve.
s: Respiratory distress due to phrenic nerve palsy

P15.d: Other birth injuries, such as liver, spleen, eye and sternocleidomastoid injury.

P20.d: Insufficient fetal oxygenation during pregnancy or labor, detected by changes in fetal well-being.

P21.d: Failure of gas exchange at birth with hypoxemia, hypercapnia and acidosis, which may cause encephalopathy.

P22.d: Breathing difficulty in the newborn, such as hyaline membrane disease and transient tachypnea.

P23.d: Pneumonia acquired in utero or during delivery, caused by viruses, bacteria or other agents.

P24.d: Aspiration of meconium, blood, amniotic fluid or milk by the newborn, with airway obstruction and pulmonary inflammation.

P25.n: Interstitial emphysema and related conditions originating in the perinatal period
P25.d: Air leak from the alveoli into the interstitium or the pleural, mediastinal or pericardial spaces in the perinatal period.

P26.n: Pulmonary haemorrhage originating in the perinatal period
P26.d: Pulmonary bleeding in the newborn, usually in severely ill preterm infants or those with asphyxia.
s: Bloody secretions from the endotracheal tube

P27.n: Chronic respiratory disease originating in the perinatal period
P27.d: Chronic neonatal lung disease, mainly bronchopulmonary dysplasia in ventilated preterm infants.

P28.n: Other respiratory conditions originating in the perinatal period
P28.d: Other perinatal respiratory conditions, such as apnea of prematurity, atelectasis and respiratory failure.

P29.n: Cardiovascular disorders originating in the perinatal period
P29.d: Perinatal cardiovascular disorders, such as persistent pulmonary hypertension, arrhythmias and neonatal heart failure.

P35.d: Viral infections acquired in utero, such as congenital rubella and congenital cytomegalovirus infection.

P36.d: Systemic bacterial infection of the newborn, early- or late-onset, caused by group B streptococcus, E. coli and others.

P37.n: Other congenital infectious and parasitic diseases
P37.d: Other congenital infections, such as congenital toxoplasmosis, tuberculosis, malaria and candidiasis.

P38.n: Omphalitis of newborn with or without mild haemorrhage
P38.d: Infection of the newborn's umbilical stump, which may extend to the abdominal wall.

P39.n: Other infections specific to the perinatal period
P39.d: Other perinatal infections, such as neonatal mastitis, neonatal conjunctivitis and urinary tract infection.

P50.d: Blood loss from the fetus, such as fetomaternal hemorrhage, vasa previa and twin-to-twin transfusion.

P51.d: Bleeding from the umbilical stump in the newborn.

P52.n: Intracranial nontraumatic haemorrhage of fetus and newborn
P52.d: Nontraumatic intracranial hemorrhage, mainly periventricular-intraventricular in preterm infants.

P53.n: Haemorrhagic disease of fetus and newborn
P53.d: Bleeding due to vitamin K deficiency in the newborn.

P54.d: Other neonatal hemorrhages, such as hematemesis, melena and adrenal hemorrhage.

P55.n: Haemolytic disease of fetus and newborn
P55.d: Fetal or neonatal hemolysis due to maternal antibodies against red cell antigens, such as Rh or ABO.

P56.n: Hydrops fetalis due to haemolytic disease
P56.d: Generalized fetal edema due to severe anemia secondary to alloimmune hemolytic disease.

P57.d: Encephalopathy due to deposition of indirect bilirubin in the basal ganglia.
s: Sequelae such as deafness and cerebral palsy

P58.n: Neonatal jaundice due to other excessive haemolysis
P58.d: Neonatal jaundice due to hemolysis from other causes, such as hematomas, polycythemia and drugs.

P59.n: Neonatal jaundice from other and unspecified causes
P59.d: Neonatal jaundice from other causes, such as prematurity, breast milk and unspecified causes.

P60.n: Disseminated intravascular coagulation of fetus and newborn
P60.d: Diffuse activation of coagulation in the newborn, with consumption of clotting factors and platelets, secondary to sepsis or asphyxia.

P61.d: Other perinatal hematological disorders, such as neonatal thrombocytopenia, polycythemia and anemia of prematurity.

P70.n: Transitory disorders of carbohydrate metabolism specific to fetus and newborn
P70.d: Transient blood glucose disorders of the newborn, such as hypoglycemia and infant of a diabetic mother.

P71.n: Transitory neonatal disorders of calcium and magnesium metabolism
P71.d: Transient calcium and magnesium disorders in the neonatal period, such as hypocalcemia.

P72.d: Transient neonatal endocrine disorders, such as goiter and transient hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism.

P74.n: Other transitory neonatal electrolyte and metabolic disturbances
P74.d: Transient neonatal electrolyte and metabolic disorders, such as dehydration and sodium and potassium abnormalities.

P75.d: Obstruction of the ileum by thick meconium, usually associated with cystic fibrosis.

P76.d: Other neonatal intestinal obstructions, such as meconium plug syndrome and milk impaction.

P77.n: Necrotizing enterocolitis of fetus and newborn
P77.d: Inflammatory intestinal necrosis, mainly in preterm infants, due to ischemia, immaturity and bacterial colonization.

P78.d: Other perinatal digestive disorders, such as intestinal perforation and neonatal gastroesophageal reflux.

P80.d: Body temperature below normal in the newborn, due to heat loss or inadequate heat production.

P81.n: Other disturbances of temperature regulation of newborn
P81.d: Other temperature disorders of the newborn, such as environmental hyperthermia and neonatal fever.

P83.n: Other conditions of integument specific to fetus and newborn
P83.d: Skin conditions of the newborn, such as sclerema, erythema toxicum, nonhemolytic hydrops and umbilical stump abnormalities.

P90.d: Seizures in the neonatal period, due to hypoxia, hemorrhage, infection or metabolic disorders.
s: Subtle movements such as chewing and pedaling

P91.n: Other disturbances of cerebral status of newborn
P91.d: Other neonatal brain disorders, such as cerebral ischemia, periventricular leukomalacia and hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.

P92.d: Feeding difficulties of the newborn, such as vomiting, regurgitation, rumination and weak suck.

P93.n: Reactions and intoxications due to drugs administered to fetus and newborn
P93.d: Adverse effects or intoxications in the fetus or newborn from directly administered drugs, such as gray baby syndrome.

P94.n: Disorders of muscle tone of newborn
P94.d: Abnormal muscle tone in the newborn, such as transient neonatal myasthenia gravis and congenital hypotonia.

P95.d: Records fetal death without a specified cause.

P96.n: Other conditions originating in the perinatal period
P96.d: Residual perinatal conditions, such as neonatal renal failure and neonatal abstinence syndrome due to maternal drug use.

Q00.d: Defect in closure of the cranial neural tube with absence of most of the brain and skull vault, incompatible with life.

Q01.d: Herniation of meninges and brain tissue through a bony defect of the skull, usually occipital.

Q02.d: Head circumference more than 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and sex, due to deficient brain growth.

Q03.d: Accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid with ventricular dilation present at birth, due to aqueductal stenosis or other malformations.

Q04.d: Brain malformations such as holoprosencephaly, agenesis of the corpus callosum, lissencephaly and congenital brain cysts.

Q05.d: Defect in closure of the caudal neural tube, with exposure or herniation of the meninges and spinal cord.

Q06.n: Other congenital malformations of spinal cord
Q06.d: Spinal cord malformations such as diastematomyelia, hydromyelia and tethered cord.

Q07.n: Other congenital malformations of nervous system
Q07.d: Malformations of other parts of the nervous system, such as Arnold-Chiari malformation and dysgeneses.

Q10.n: Congenital malformations of eyelid, lacrimal apparatus and orbit
Q10.d: Malformations of the eyelids, lacrimal system and orbit, such as congenital ptosis and congenital ectropion.

Q11.d: Absence or abnormal size of the eyeball, with variable visual impairment.

Q12.d: Congenital malformations of the lens, such as congenital cataract, ectopia lentis and lens coloboma.

Q13.n: Congenital malformations of anterior segment of eye
Q13.d: Malformations of the anterior segment, such as iris coloboma, aniridia and corneal anomalies.

Q14.n: Congenital malformations of posterior segment of eye
Q14.d: Malformations of the vitreous, retina, choroid and optic nerve, such as retinal coloboma and optic nerve hypoplasia.

Q15.d: Other eye malformations, such as congenital glaucoma.

Q16.n: Congenital malformations of ear causing impairment of hearing
Q16.d: Malformations of the external, middle or inner ear that lead to hearing loss.
s: Absence or atresia of the ear canal

Q17.d: Ear malformations without hearing impairment, such as preauricular tags, microtia and prominent ear.

Q18.n: Other congenital malformations of face and neck
Q18.d: Malformations of the face and neck, such as branchial fistulas, macrostomia and branchial cyst.
s: Discharge from an opening in the neck

Q20.n: Congenital malformations of cardiac chambers and connections
Q20.d: Anomalies of the cardiac chambers and their connections, such as transposition of the great arteries and truncus arteriosus.

Q21.d: Defects of the cardiac septa, such as ventricular septal defect, atrial septal defect, atrioventricular septal defect and tetralogy of Fallot.

Q22.n: Congenital malformations of pulmonary and tricuspid valves
Q22.d: Malformations of the pulmonary and tricuspid valves, such as pulmonary stenosis or atresia and Ebstein anomaly.

Q23.n: Congenital malformations of aortic and mitral valves
Q23.d: Malformations of the aortic and mitral valves, such as bicuspid aortic valve and hypoplastic left heart syndrome.
s: Shock when the ductus arteriosus closes

Q24.d: Other heart malformations, such as dextrocardia, coronary anomalies and congenital heart block.
s: Heart sounds on the right side

Q25.d: Malformations of the aorta and pulmonary artery, such as patent ductus arteriosus and coarctation of the aorta.

Q26.d: Malformations of the great veins, such as anomalous pulmonary venous drainage and persistent left superior vena cava.

Q27.n: Other congenital malformations of peripheral vascular system
Q27.d: Malformations of the peripheral vessels, such as arteriovenous malformations and absence of an umbilical artery.

Q28.n: Other congenital malformations of circulatory system
Q28.d: Other malformations of the circulatory system, such as cerebral arteriovenous malformations and congenital aneurysms.

Q30.d: Malformations of the nose, such as choanal atresia, nasal cleft and bifid nose.
s: Inability to pass a nasal catheter

Q31.d: Malformations of the larynx, such as laryngomalacia, laryngeal web and congenital subglottic stenosis.
s: Worsening in the supine position and during feeding

Q32.n: Congenital malformations of trachea and bronchus
Q32.d: Malformations of the trachea and bronchi, such as tracheomalacia, tracheal stenosis and bronchomalacia.

Q33.d: Malformations of the lung, such as congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation, pulmonary sequestration and pulmonary hypoplasia.

Q34.n: Other congenital malformations of respiratory system
Q34.d: Other malformations of the respiratory system, such as anomalies of the pleura and mediastinum.

Q35.d: Failure of fusion of the palatal shelves during the embryonic period, creating a communication between the oral and nasal cavities.
s: Cleft visible in the palate on examination

Q36.d: Failure of fusion of the maxillary and medial nasal processes, producing a unilateral or bilateral cleft of the upper lip.
s: Cleft of the upper lip visible at birth
Difficulty forming a seal when sucking
Dental abnormalities in the cleft region

Q37.d: Combined cleft of the upper lip and palate due to failure of fusion of the embryonic facial processes.

Q38.n: Other congenital malformations of tongue, mouth and pharynx
Q38.d: Developmental anomalies of the tongue, mouth and pharynx, such as ankyloglossia, macroglossia and pharyngeal pouches.
s: Short lingual frenulum limiting the tongue

Q39.d: Defects of tracheoesophageal separation or of the esophageal lumen, such as esophageal atresia and tracheoesophageal fistula.
s: Coughing, cyanosis and choking during feeds
Inability to pass a gastric tube

Q40.n: Other congenital malformations of upper alimentary tract
Q40.d: Anomalies of the stomach and proximal duodenum, such as hypertrophic pyloric stenosis, congenital hiatal hernia and duplications.

Q41.n: Congenital absence, atresia and stenosis of small intestine
Q41.d: Congenital interruption or narrowing of the lumen of the duodenum, jejunum or ileum, usually due to a vascular event or failure of recanalization.
s: Bilious vomiting in the first hours of life
Absent or delayed passage of meconium
Double bubble sign in the duodenum

Q42.n: Congenital absence, atresia and stenosis of large intestine
Q42.d: Congenital absence or narrowing of the colonic lumen, causing low intestinal obstruction in the newborn.

Q43.d: Intestinal anomalies such as Meckel diverticulum, Hirschsprung disease, malrotation and anorectal malformations.

Q44.n: Congenital malformations of gallbladder, bile ducts and liver
Q44.d: Hepatobiliary developmental anomalies, such as biliary atresia, choledochal cyst and gallbladder agenesis.
s: Prolonged cholestatic jaundice in the infant

Q45.n: Other congenital malformations of digestive system
Q45.d: Anomalies of other digestive organs, such as annular pancreas, ectopic pancreas and duplications of the digestive tract.

Q50.n: Congenital malformations of ovaries, fallopian tubes and broad ligaments
Q50.d: Developmental anomalies of the ovaries, fallopian tubes and broad ligaments, such as agenesis, accessory ovary and embryonic cysts.
s: Amenorrhea or infertility in some cases

Q51.n: Congenital malformations of uterus and cervix
Q51.d: Failure of development or fusion of the Müllerian ducts, producing a didelphic, bicornuate or septate uterus or uterine agenesis.

Q52.n: Other congenital malformations of female genitalia
Q52.d: Anomalies of the vagina, hymen, vulva and clitoris, such as vaginal agenesis, vaginal septum and imperforate hymen.
s: Dyspareunia or inability to have intercourse

Q53.d: Failure of the testis to migrate to the scrotum; it may remain in the abdomen or the inguinal canal.
s: Testis palpable in the inguinal canal

Q54.d: Ectopic opening of the urethral meatus on the ventral surface of the penis, scrotum or perineum, due to incomplete fusion of the urethral folds.

Q55.n: Other congenital malformations of male genital organs
Q55.d: Anomalies of the penis, scrotum and testes, such as micropenis, testicular agenesis, retractile testis and scrotal anomalies.

Q56.d: External genitalia that are ambiguous or discordant with chromosomal/gonadal sex, due to disorders of sex development.
s: Fluid and electrolyte disturbances in adrenal hyperplasia

Q60.n: Renal agenesis and other reduction defects of kidney
Q60.d: Congenital absence or hypoplasia of one or both kidneys; the bilateral form is incompatible with life.
s: Severe oligohydramnios in the bilateral form
Compensatory solitary kidney in the unilateral form

Q61.d: Kidney diseases with cyst formation, such as autosomal dominant and recessive polycystic kidney disease and multicystic dysplasia.

Q62.n: Congenital obstructive defects of renal pelvis and congenital malformations of ureter
Q62.d: Congenital obstructive anomalies of the ureteropelvic junction and ureter, such as stenosis, megaureter and ureterocele.

Q63.d: Anomalies of kidney shape, position or number, such as horseshoe kidney, renal ectopia and supernumerary kidney.
s: Increased risk of stones and urinary tract infection

Q64.n: Other congenital malformations of urinary system
Q64.d: Anomalies of the bladder and urethra, such as bladder exstrophy, posterior urethral valves and congenital diverticula.

Q65.d: Developmental dysplasia of the hip, with instability or displacement of the femoral head relative to the acetabulum.
s: Asymmetry of gluteal and thigh folds

Q66.d: Postural or structural deformities of the foot present at birth, such as congenital clubfoot, metatarsus varus and flatfoot.

Q67.n: Congenital musculoskeletal deformities of head, face, spine and chest
Q67.d: Congenital deformities of the head, face, spine and chest, such as plagiocephaly, facial asymmetry, postural scoliosis and pectus excavatum and carinatum.
s: Depression or protrusion of the sternum

Q68.d: Other congenital musculoskeletal deformities, such as congenital torticollis, congenital dislocation of the knee and bowing of long bones.
s: Neck tilt with a nodule in the sternocleidomastoid

Q69.d: Presence of supernumerary fingers or toes, isolated or associated with genetic syndromes.
s: Duplication of the thumb or great toe

Q70.d: Congenital fusion of adjacent digits, cutaneous or bony, due to failure of interdigital apoptosis.
s: Bony fusion in the complex form
Limited movement of the involved digits

Q71.d: Congenital total or partial absence of upper limb segments, such as amelia, phocomelia and hemimelia.
s: Absence of part of the arm, forearm or hand

Q72.d: Congenital total or partial absence of lower limb segments, such as proximal focal femoral deficiency and fibular or tibial hemimelia.
s: Absence of bones or rays of the foot

Q73.d: Congenital limb reduction defects without specification of upper or lower limb, such as unspecified amelia or phocomelia.
s: Total or partial absence of a limb

Q74.d: Other congenital anomalies of the limbs and the shoulder or pelvic girdle, such as arthrogryposis and radioulnar synostosis.

Q75.n: Other congenital malformations of skull and face bones
Q75.d: Bony anomalies of the skull and face, such as craniosynostosis, craniofacial dysostosis and hypertelorism.

Q76.n: Congenital malformations of spine and bony thorax
Q76.d: Congenital anomalies of the vertebrae, ribs and sternum, such as spina bifida occulta, hemivertebra, cervical rib and Klippel-Feil.

Q77.n: Osteochondrodysplasia with defects of growth of tubular bones and spine
Q77.d: Skeletal dysplasias affecting growth of the long bones and spine, such as achondroplasia and thanatophoric dysplasia.

Q78.d: Other bone dysplasias, such as osteogenesis imperfecta, osteopetrosis and multiple exostoses.

Q79.n: Congenital malformations of the musculoskeletal system, not elsewhere classified
Q79.d: Various congenital musculoskeletal anomalies, such as diaphragmatic hernia, omphalocele, gastroschisis and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
s: Abdominal wall defect with exposed viscera
Neonatal respiratory distress in diaphragmatic hernia

Q80.d: Inherited disorders of keratinization with generalized scaling of the skin from birth.
s: Ectropion and eclabium in severe forms

Q81.d: Genodermatoses caused by defects in adhesion proteins of the dermoepidermal junction, with fragility of the skin and mucous membranes.

Q82.d: Other congenital skin anomalies, such as port-wine stains, congenital nevi, hereditary lymphedema and cutaneous mastocytosis.

Q83.d: Congenital breast anomalies, such as amastia, accessory breasts and supernumerary nipples.
s: Extra nipple or breast tissue along the milk line

Q84.d: Congenital anomalies of the skin appendages and integument, such as congenital alopecia, nail anomalies and aplasia cutis.
s: Area of absent skin on the scalp

Q85.d: Neurocutaneous syndromes with hamartomas in the skin, nervous system and other organs, such as neurofibromatosis and tuberous sclerosis.

Q86.n: Congenital malformation syndromes due to known exogenous causes, not elsewhere classified
Q86.d: Malformation syndromes caused by exogenous agents during pregnancy, such as alcohol, hydantoin and warfarin.
s: Smooth philtrum and thin upper lip with alcohol

Q87.n: Other specified congenital malformation syndromes affecting multiple systems
Q87.d: Genetic syndromes with malformations in several systems, such as Marfan, Noonan, Prader-Willi and Beckwith-Wiedemann.

Q89.n: Other congenital malformations, not elsewhere classified
Q89.d: Congenital malformations not classified in other groups, such as asplenia, situs inversus and conjoined twins, as well as unspecified malformations.

Q90.d: Aneuploidy due to an extra copy of chromosome 21, usually free trisomy, with intellectual disability and malformations.
s: Upslanting palpebral fissures and single palmar crease

Q91.d: Trisomies of chromosome 18 (Edwards) and 13 (Patau), with severe malformations and high mortality in the first year.
s: Clenched hands with overlapping fingers in Edwards
Cleft lip and palate and polydactyly in Patau

Q92.n: Other trisomies and partial trisomies of the autosomes, not elsewhere classified
Q92.d: Rare autosomal trisomies, complete, partial or mosaic, other than those of chromosomes 13, 18 and 21.

Q93.n: Monosomies and deletions from the autosomes, not elsewhere classified
Q93.d: Loss of an autosomal chromosome or chromosome segment, such as cri du chat, Wolf-Hirschhorn and Angelman.

Q95.n: Balanced rearrangements and structural markers, not elsewhere classified
Q95.d: Balanced translocations and inversions without loss of genetic material; the carrier is usually healthy, with reproductive risk.

Q96.d: Total or partial monosomy of the X chromosome (45,X or mosaics) in a female phenotype, with gonadal dysgenesis.
s: Coarctation of the aorta and bicuspid aortic valve

Q97.n: Other sex chromosome abnormalities, female phenotype, not elsewhere classified
Q97.d: X chromosome aneuploidies in a female phenotype, such as 47,XXX, often with a mild clinical picture.
s: Premature ovarian insufficiency in some cases

Q98.n: Other sex chromosome abnormalities, male phenotype, not elsewhere classified
Q98.d: Sex chromosome aneuploidies in a male phenotype, such as Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) and 47,XYY.

Q99.n: Other chromosome abnormalities, not elsewhere classified
Q99.d: Other chromosomal anomalies not specified elsewhere, such as chimeras and fragile X chromosome.
s: Long face and large ears in fragile X

R00.d: Changes in heart rate or rhythm perceived or detected without a diagnosis of a specific arrhythmia, such as tachycardia, bradycardia and palpitations.

R01.n: Cardiac murmurs and other cardiac sounds
R01.d: Heart murmurs and sounds detected on auscultation without a defined structural diagnosis, innocent or still under investigation.

R02.d: Tissue necrosis due to ischemia, with or without infection, without a specific classified cause, usually in the extremities.
s: Foul-smelling discharge in the wet form

R03.d: Record of an isolated high or low blood pressure reading, without an established diagnosis of hypertension or hypotension.
s: Low blood pressure reading without symptoms

R04.d: Bleeding originating in the airways, from the nose to the lungs, without a defined etiologic diagnosis.

R05.d: Protective expulsive reflex of the airways, acute or chronic, recorded when the cause is not defined.
s: Cough persisting for more than 8 weeks in the chronic form

R06.d: Changes in breathing pattern without a defined diagnosis, such as dyspnea, stridor, wheezing, hiccups and hyperventilation.

R07.d: Throat or chest pain without an established cause, including atypical chest pain and pain on breathing.

R09.n: Other symptoms and signs involving the circulatory and respiratory systems
R09.d: Other cardiorespiratory signs without a defined diagnosis, such as asphyxia, pleurisy, respiratory arrest and abnormal sputum.

R10.d: Pain localized in the abdomen or pelvis without an etiologic diagnosis yet, including acute abdomen and colic.

R11.d: Sensation of gastric discomfort with retching and expulsion of gastric contents, recorded without a defined cause.

R12.d: Rising retrosternal burning sensation, usually due to acid reflux, recorded without a defined diagnosis.
s: Worse after meals and when lying down

R13.d: Difficulty swallowing solids or liquids, of oropharyngeal or esophageal origin, without a defined cause.

R14.d: Excess gas in the digestive tract, with distension, belching and passing of flatus.

R15.d: Involuntary loss of stool or gas due to failure of the sphincter mechanism or of rectal sensation.

R16.n: Hepatomegaly and splenomegaly, not elsewhere classified
R16.d: Enlargement of the liver and/or spleen detected on examination or imaging, without a defined etiologic diagnosis.
s: Liver palpable below the costal margin

R17.d: Yellowish discoloration of the skin and mucous membranes due to hyperbilirubinemia, without a defined cause.

R18.d: Accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity, due to portal hypertension, neoplasm, infection or hypoalbuminemia, without a defined cause.

R19.n: Other symptoms and signs involving the digestive system and abdomen
R19.d: Other digestive and abdominal signs without a diagnosis, such as abdominal mass, change in bowel habits and abnormal bowel sounds.

R20.d: Changes in skin sensation without a defined neurological diagnosis, such as anesthesia, hypoesthesia and paresthesia.

R21.n: Rash and other nonspecific skin eruption
R21.d: Nonspecific skin eruption or redness without a defined dermatological diagnosis.

R22.n: Localized swelling, mass and lump of skin and subcutaneous tissue
R22.d: Localized swelling in the skin or subcutaneous tissue, not yet diagnosed.

R23.d: Other skin changes without a diagnosis, such as cyanosis, pallor, flushing, petechiae and changes in texture.

R25.d: Involuntary movements without a specific neurological diagnosis, such as tremor, cramp, fasciculation and spasm.

R26.d: Changes in gait and walking ability without a defined cause, including ataxic gait, spastic gait and immobility.

R27.d: Motor incoordination without a defined neurological diagnosis, such as ataxia and dysmetria.

R29.n: Other symptoms and signs involving the nervous and musculoskeletal systems
R29.d: Other neurological and musculoskeletal signs without a diagnosis, such as tetany, meningismus, abnormal reflexes and repeated falls.

R30.d: Pain or discomfort when urinating, usually due to inflammation or infection of the lower urinary tract, without a defined diagnosis.

R31.d: Presence of blood in the urine, gross or microscopic, without a defined cause.
s: Red blood cells in the urine sediment
Associated flank pain in some cases

R32.d: Involuntary loss of urine without a defined type or cause.

R33.d: Inability to empty the bladder, acute or chronic, due to obstruction, drugs or neurological dysfunction.

R34.d: Marked reduction (oliguria) or absence (anuria) of urine output, without a defined diagnosis.
s: Urine output below 100 mL/day in anuria

R35.d: Increased daily urine volume, due to osmotic diuresis, diabetes insipidus or excessive intake, without a defined cause.

R36.d: Discharge from the urethra, usually of infectious origin, without an etiologic diagnosis yet.

R39.n: Other symptoms and signs involving the urinary system
R39.d: Other urinary signs without a diagnosis, such as urgency, hesitancy, frequency, nocturia and urine extravasation.

R40.d: Decreased level of consciousness of varying degrees, from drowsiness to coma, without a defined cause.

R41.n: Other symptoms and signs involving cognitive functions and awareness
R41.d: Cognitive and consciousness changes without a defined diagnosis, such as disorientation, amnesia and confusion.

R42.d: Sensation of dizziness or imbalance without a defined vestibular or cardiovascular diagnosis.

R43.d: Loss or alteration of smell and taste, without a defined cause.

R44.n: Other symptoms and signs involving general sensations and perceptions
R44.d: Perceptual disturbances without a defined psychiatric or neurological diagnosis, such as hallucinations.

R45.n: Symptoms and signs involving emotional state
R45.d: Isolated emotional signs without a psychiatric diagnosis, such as nervousness, irritability, sadness and suicidal ideation.

R46.n: Symptoms and signs involving appearance and behaviour
R46.d: Changes in appearance and behavior without a psychiatric diagnosis, such as personal neglect, suspiciousness and strange behavior.

R47.d: Speech disturbances without a defined diagnosis, such as dysphasia, dysarthria and aphasia.

R48.n: Dyslexia and other symbolic dysfunctions, not elsewhere classified
R48.d: Acquired disorders of reading, writing and symbolization, such as dyslexia, agnosia, apraxia and alexia.

R49.d: Voice changes without a defined diagnosis, such as hoarseness, aphonia and hypernasality.

R50.n: Fever of other and unknown origin
R50.d: Elevated body temperature without an identified focus or cause, including persistent fever and postprocedural fever.

R51.d: Head pain without a diagnosis of a specific headache syndrome.

R52.d: Acute or chronic pain without a location or cause classified elsewhere.

R53.d: Sensation of tiredness, weakness and general malaise without a defined diagnosis.

R54.d: Functional decline associated with aging, without psychosis, with frailty and reduced physiological reserve.
s: Weakness and loss of muscle mass

R55.d: Transient loss of consciousness and postural tone due to global cerebral hypoperfusion, with spontaneous recovery.
s: Prodrome of dizziness and blurred vision

R56.d: Seizures without a diagnosis of epilepsy, including febrile and post-traumatic seizures.

R57.d: Circulatory failure with tissue hypoperfusion, such as cardiogenic or hypovolemic shock, not classified elsewhere.

R58.d: Bleeding without a location or cause specified elsewhere in the classification.

R59.d: Localized or generalized lymph node enlargement, without a defined diagnosis.

R60.d: Localized or generalized accumulation of interstitial fluid without a defined cause.

R61.d: Localized or generalized excessive sweating beyond thermoregulatory needs.
s: Excessive sweating of the hands and armpits

R62.n: Lack of expected normal physiological development
R62.d: Delay in growth or in the developmental milestones expected for age, without a defined cause.

R63.n: Symptoms and signs concerning food and fluid intake
R63.d: Changes in food or fluid intake, such as anorexia, polydipsia, polyphagia and abnormal weight loss or gain.

R64.d: Severe wasting state with loss of muscle mass and fat due to chronic disease, neoplasm or inflammation.

R68.d: Other general signs without a diagnosis, such as non-environmental hypothermia, chills, digital clubbing and dry mouth.

R69.n: Unknown and unspecified causes of morbidity
R69.d: Records illness or morbidity whose cause is unknown or unspecified; used when no diagnostic information is available.

R70.n: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and abnormality of plasma viscosity
R70.d: Increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate or plasma viscosity, a nonspecific marker of inflammation or paraprotein.
s: Association with inflammation, infection or neoplasm

R71.d: Morphological or quantitative abnormalities of red blood cells without a diagnosis of a specific anemia.

R72.n: Abnormality of white blood cells, not elsewhere classified
R72.d: Abnormalities of white blood cell count or morphology without a defined diagnosis.

R73.d: Blood glucose above normal without a diagnosis of diabetes, including impaired fasting glucose and glucose intolerance.
s: 2-h glucose between 140 and 199 on the OGTT

R74.d: Abnormalities of serum enzymes without a diagnosis, such as elevated transaminases, LDH, amylase and alkaline phosphatase.

R75.n: Laboratory evidence of human immunodeficiency virus [HIV]
R75.d: Records a positive or inconclusive laboratory test for HIV without a confirmed diagnosis, common in infants born to seropositive mothers.

R76.n: Other abnormal immunological findings in serum
R76.d: Abnormal serum immunological findings, such as a raised antibody titer, positive tuberculin test and false-positive syphilis test.

R77.d: Abnormalities of plasma proteins without a diagnosis, such as hypoalbuminemia and globulin abnormalities.

R78.n: Findings of drugs and other substances, not normally found in blood
R78.d: Records detection in the blood of alcohol, drugs, medications, heavy metals or other substances normally absent.

R79.n: Other abnormal findings of blood chemistry
R79.d: Other abnormal chemical findings in the blood, such as mineral and blood gas abnormalities without a defined diagnosis.

R80.d: Isolated presence of protein in the urine without diagnosed kidney disease, including orthostatic proteinuria.
s: Proteinuria on dipstick or quantitative testing

R81.d: Presence of glucose in the urine without a diagnosis of diabetes or of defined renal glycosuria.

R82.d: Other abnormal findings in the urine, such as ketonuria, hemoglobinuria, myoglobinuria, bilirubinuria and bacteriuria.

R83.d: Abnormalities in the cerebrospinal fluid without a diagnosis, such as abnormal cell count, protein, glucose or cytology.

R84.n: Abnormal findings in specimens from respiratory organs and thorax
R84.d: Abnormal findings in sputum, bronchial washings, pleural fluid or nasal secretions without a defined diagnosis.

R85.n: Abnormal findings in specimens from digestive organs and abdominal cavity
R85.d: Abnormal findings in digestive and peritoneal material, such as ascitic fluid, saliva and secretions, without a defined diagnosis.

R86.n: Abnormal findings in specimens from male genital organs
R86.d: Abnormal findings in material from the male genital organs, such as semen and prostatic secretions, without a defined diagnosis.

R87.n: Abnormal findings in specimens from female genital organs
R87.d: Abnormal findings in female genital material, particularly cytological abnormalities of the cervix on Pap smear screening.

R89.n: Abnormal findings in specimens from other organs, systems and tissues
R89.d: Abnormal findings in material from other organs and tissues, such as synovial fluid, wound secretions and skin.

R90.n: Abnormal findings on diagnostic imaging of central nervous system
R90.d: Abnormal findings on CT, MRI or other imaging of the central nervous system without a defined diagnosis.

R91.n: Abnormal findings on diagnostic imaging of lung
R91.d: Abnormal findings on chest radiograph or CT of the lung without a diagnosis, such as a solitary pulmonary nodule.

R92.n: Abnormal findings on diagnostic imaging of breast
R92.d: Abnormal findings on mammography or other breast imaging without a defined diagnosis, usually categorized by BI-RADS.

R93.n: Abnormal findings on diagnostic imaging of other body structures
R93.d: Abnormal findings on imaging of other structures, such as the heart, liver, biliary tract, urinary tract and bone, without a diagnosis.
s: Liver or biliary lesion on imaging

R94.d: Abnormal results of functional tests, such as electroencephalogram, electrocardiogram, spirometry, and liver, kidney or thyroid function tests.
s: Abnormal thyroid or kidney function tests

R95.d: Sudden, unexplained death of an infant under 1 year of age, usually during sleep, with no cause found after a complete investigation.

R96.d: Records sudden death, instantaneous or within 24 h of symptom onset, with no identified cause.

R98.d: Records a death found or occurring without witnesses and without medical care, when the cause cannot be determined.

R99.n: Other ill-defined and unspecified causes of mortality
R99.d: Records death from an ill-defined or unknown cause, without sufficient information to classify the underlying cause.

S00.d: Traumatic injury limited to the skin and subcutaneous tissue of the head, such as abrasion, contusion and hematoma, without an open wound.

S01.d: Traumatic break in the skin of the head, including the scalp, eyelid, ear, nose and mouth.

S02.n: Fracture of skull and facial bones
S02.d: Fracture of the skull vault, skull base or facial bones from direct trauma, with risk of associated brain injury.

S03.n: Dislocation, sprain and strain of joints and ligaments of head
S03.d: Injury to joints and ligaments of the head, such as dislocation of the jaw and sprain of the temporomandibular joint.

S04.d: Traumatic injury of cranial nerves, such as the optic, oculomotor, trigeminal and facial nerves.

S05.d: Traumatic injury of the eyeball and orbit, such as corneal abrasion, contusion, laceration and ocular perforation.

S06.d: Traumatic brain injury, such as concussion, contusion, epidural and subdural hematoma, and traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage.

S07.d: Compression injury of the head with soft tissue and bone damage, often severe.

S08.n: Traumatic amputation of part of head
S08.d: Traumatic loss of part of the head, such as scalping, or loss of the ear or nose.

S09.n: Other and unspecified injuries of head
S09.d: Other and unspecified injuries of the head, such as injury of cranial muscles and vessels and head trauma without further detail.

S10.d: Superficial traumatic injury of the neck, such as contusion, abrasion and hematoma, without an open wound.

S11.d: Open wound of the neck, with risk of injury to the larynx, trachea, thyroid, pharynx or esophagus.

S12.d: Fracture of the cervical vertebrae from trauma, with risk of spinal cord injury.

S13.n: Dislocation, sprain and strain of joints and ligaments at neck level
S13.d: Dislocation or ligament injury of the cervical spine, including whiplash-type cervical sprain.

S14.n: Injury of nerves and spinal cord at neck level
S14.d: Traumatic injury of the cervical spinal cord or of nerve roots and brachial plexus, with motor and sensory deficit.

S15.n: Injury of blood vessels at neck level
S15.d: Traumatic injury of the carotid or vertebral arteries or jugular veins.

S16.n: Injury of muscle and tendon at neck level
S16.d: Traumatic injury of cervical muscles and tendons, such as muscle strain.

S17.d: Compression injury of the neck, with damage to the larynx, trachea or vessels.

S18.d: Traumatic amputation at neck level, including decapitation.

S19.n: Other and unspecified injuries of neck
S19.d: Other and unspecified injuries of the neck, such as injuries of multiple cervical structures without further detail.

S20.d: Superficial injury of the thorax, such as contusion of the chest wall or breast, without an open wound.

S21.d: Open wound of the chest wall, with or without penetration into the pleural cavity.

S22.n: Fracture of rib(s), sternum and thoracic spine
S22.d: Fracture of the ribs, sternum or thoracic vertebrae, including flail chest.
s: Chest pain that varies with breathing

S23.n: Dislocation, sprain and strain of joints and ligaments of thorax
S23.d: Dislocation or ligament injury of the thoracic spine, ribs and sternum.

S24.n: Injury of nerves and spinal cord at thorax level
S24.d: Traumatic injury of the thoracic spinal cord or thoracic nerves.

S25.n: Injury of blood vessels of thorax
S25.d: Traumatic injury of the thoracic aorta, vena cava, or pulmonary and intercostal vessels.

S26.d: Traumatic injury of the heart, such as myocardial contusion, laceration and hemopericardium.

S27.n: Injury of other and unspecified intrathoracic organs
S27.d: Injury of the lung, pleura, trachea, bronchi, esophagus or diaphragm, such as traumatic pneumothorax and hemothorax.

S28.n: Crushing injury of thorax and traumatic amputation of part of thorax
S28.d: Crushing injury of the thorax or traumatic amputation of part of it, including the breast.

S29.n: Other and unspecified injuries of thorax
S29.d: Other and unspecified injuries of the thorax, such as muscle injuries of the chest wall.

S30.n: Superficial injury of abdomen, lower back and pelvis
S30.d: Superficial injury of the abdomen, back, pelvis and external genitalia, without an open wound.

S31.n: Open wound of abdomen, lower back and pelvis
S31.d: Open wound of the abdomen, back, pelvis or external genitalia, with or without peritoneal penetration.

S32.n: Fracture of lumbar spine and pelvis
S32.d: Fracture of the lumbar vertebrae, sacrum or pelvic bones, with risk of major hemorrhage.

S33.n: Dislocation, sprain and strain of joints and ligaments of lumbar spine and pelvis
S33.d: Dislocation or ligament injury of the lumbar spine, sacroiliac joint and pubic symphysis.

S34.n: Injury of nerves and lumbar spinal cord at abdomen, lower back and pelvis level
S34.d: Traumatic injury of the lumbar spinal cord, cauda equina or lumbosacral nerves.

S35.n: Injury of blood vessels at abdomen, lower back and pelvis level
S35.d: Traumatic injury of the abdominal aorta, vena cava, iliac or visceral vessels.

S36.d: Traumatic injury of the spleen, liver, pancreas, stomach or intestine.

S37.n: Injury of urinary and pelvic organs
S37.d: Traumatic injury of the kidney, ureter, bladder, urethra or internal pelvic organs.

S38.n: Crushing injury and traumatic amputation of part of abdomen, lower back and pelvis
S38.d: Crushing injury or traumatic amputation of part of the abdomen, back, pelvis or external genitalia.

S39.n: Other and unspecified injuries of abdomen, lower back and pelvis
S39.d: Other and unspecified injuries of the abdomen, back and pelvis, such as lumbar muscle strain.

S40.n: Superficial injury of shoulder and upper arm
S40.d: Superficial injury of the shoulder and upper arm, such as contusion and abrasion, without an open wound.

S41.n: Open wound of shoulder and upper arm
S41.d: Open wound of the shoulder and upper arm from a cut, puncture or laceration.

S42.n: Fracture of shoulder and upper arm
S42.d: Fracture of the clavicle, scapula or humerus, usually from a fall or direct trauma.
s: Loss of function of the limb
Radial nerve injury in humeral shaft fracture

S43.n: Dislocation, sprain and strain of joints and ligaments of shoulder girdle
S43.d: Dislocation or ligament injury of the shoulder, acromioclavicular and sternoclavicular joints.
s: Squared-off (epaulette) shoulder deformity in anterior dislocation

S44.n: Injury of nerves at shoulder and upper arm level
S44.d: Traumatic injury of the axillary, median, ulnar, radial or musculocutaneous nerves at the shoulder and upper arm level.
s: Wrist drop in radial nerve injury
Deltoid atrophy in axillary nerve injury

S45.n: Injury of blood vessels at shoulder and upper arm level
S45.d: Traumatic injury of the axillary or brachial artery or veins of the shoulder and upper arm.
s: Pallor and coldness of the hand

S46.n: Injury of muscle and tendon at shoulder and upper arm level
S46.d: Injury of tendons and muscles of the shoulder and upper arm, such as rotator cuff and biceps tears.

S47.n: Crushing injury of shoulder and upper arm
S47.d: Crushing injury of the shoulder and upper arm with soft tissue damage and risk of compartment syndrome.

S48.n: Traumatic amputation of shoulder and upper arm
S48.d: Traumatic loss of the upper limb at the shoulder or upper arm level.

S49.n: Other and unspecified injuries of shoulder and upper arm
S49.d: Other and unspecified injuries of the shoulder and upper arm, including multiple injuries of the region.

S50.d: Superficial injury of the elbow and forearm, such as contusion and abrasion.

S51.d: Open wound of the elbow and forearm from a cut, puncture or laceration, with risk of tendon and nerve injury.

S52.d: Fracture of the radius and/or ulna, including distal radius (Colles) fracture and olecranon fractures.
s: Loss of function of the wrist or forearm

S53.n: Dislocation, sprain and strain of joints and ligaments of elbow
S53.d: Dislocation or ligament injury of the elbow, including subluxation of the radial head (nursemaid's elbow).
s: Arm held in pronation and slight flexion in children

S54.n: Injury of nerves at forearm level
S54.d: Traumatic injury of the ulnar, median or radial nerves at forearm level.
s: Sensory loss in the nerve territory

S55.n: Injury of blood vessels at forearm level
S55.d: Traumatic injury of the radial or ulnar artery or veins of the forearm.

S56.n: Injury of muscle and tendon at forearm level
S56.d: Injury of flexor or extensor muscles and tendons at forearm level.
s: Loss of finger flexion or extension

S57.d: Crushing injury of the forearm, with risk of compartment syndrome.

S58.d: Traumatic loss of the upper limb at the elbow or forearm level.

S59.n: Other and unspecified injuries of forearm
S59.d: Other and unspecified injuries of the forearm, including multiple injuries of the region.

S60.n: Superficial injury of wrist and hand
S60.d: Superficial injury of the wrist, hand and fingers, such as contusion, abrasion and subungual hematoma.

S61.n: Open wound of wrist and hand
S61.d: Open wound of the wrist, hand or fingers, with or without nail injury.

S62.n: Fracture at wrist and hand level
S62.d: Fracture of the carpal bones, metacarpals or phalanges, such as scaphoid fracture and boxer's fracture.
s: Anatomical snuffbox tenderness in scaphoid fracture

S63.n: Dislocation, sprain and strain of joints and ligaments at wrist and hand level
S63.d: Dislocation or ligament injury of the wrist and fingers, such as sprain and injury of the thumb collateral ligament.

S64.n: Injury of nerves at wrist and hand level
S64.d: Traumatic injury of the digital, median, ulnar or radial nerves at wrist and hand level.

S65.n: Injury of blood vessels at wrist and hand level
S65.d: Traumatic injury of the palmar arches or radial, ulnar or digital arteries.

S66.n: Injury of muscle and tendon at wrist and hand level
S66.d: Injury of flexor or extensor tendons and intrinsic muscles at wrist and hand level.
s: Inability to flex or extend the finger

S67.n: Crushing injury of wrist and hand
S67.d: Compression injury of the wrist, hand or fingers, with damage to soft tissues, bones and nail bed.

S68.n: Traumatic amputation of wrist and hand
S68.d: Traumatic loss of finger(s) or of part of the hand or wrist.

S69.n: Other and unspecified injuries of wrist and hand
S69.d: Other and unspecified injuries of the wrist and hand, including multiple injuries of the region.

S70.n: Superficial injury of hip and thigh
S70.d: Superficial injury of the hip and thigh, such as contusion and abrasion.

S71.n: Open wound of hip and thigh
S71.d: Open wound of the hip and thigh from a cut, puncture or laceration, with risk of femoral vascular injury.

S72.d: Fracture of the femoral neck, trochanteric region or shaft, common in older adults after a fall.
s: Shortening and external rotation of the limb
Significant blood loss in shaft fracture

S73.n: Dislocation, sprain and strain of joint and ligaments of hip
S73.d: Dislocation or ligament injury of the hip, usually from high-energy trauma.
s: Limb shortened, adducted and internally rotated in posterior dislocation

S74.n: Injury of nerves at hip and thigh level
S74.d: Traumatic injury of the sciatic, femoral or cutaneous nerves at hip and thigh level.

S75.n: Injury of blood vessels at hip and thigh level
S75.d: Traumatic injury of the femoral artery or vein at hip and thigh level.

S76.n: Injury of muscle and tendon at hip and thigh level
S76.d: Injury of muscles and tendons of the hip and thigh, such as hamstring and quadriceps strain.

S77.n: Crushing injury of hip and thigh
S77.d: Crushing injury of the hip and thigh, with risk of rhabdomyolysis and compartment syndrome.

S78.n: Traumatic amputation of hip and thigh
S78.d: Traumatic loss of the lower limb at the hip or thigh level.

S79.n: Other and unspecified injuries of hip and thigh
S79.d: Other and unspecified injuries of the hip and thigh, including multiple injuries of the region.

S80.d: Superficial injury of the knee and lower leg, such as contusion and abrasion.

S81.d: Open wound of the knee and lower leg from a cut, puncture or laceration, with risk of infection and tibial bone exposure.

S82.n: Fracture of lower leg, including ankle
S82.d: Fracture of the patella, tibia, fibula or malleoli, including ankle fractures.
s: Risk of compartment syndrome in tibial fracture

S83.n: Dislocation, sprain and strain of joints and ligaments of knee
S83.d: Dislocation or ligament and meniscal injury of the knee, such as anterior cruciate ligament tear and meniscal injury.
s: Positive anterior drawer or Lachman test

S84.n: Injury of nerves at lower leg level
S84.d: Traumatic injury of the tibial, fibular or cutaneous nerves at lower leg level.
s: Foot drop in fibular nerve injury

S85.n: Injury of blood vessels at lower leg level
S85.d: Traumatic injury of the popliteal or tibial arteries or veins of the lower leg.
s: Pallor and coldness of the foot

S86.n: Injury of muscle and tendon at lower leg level
S86.d: Injury of muscles and tendons of the lower leg, such as Achilles tendon rupture.

S87.d: Crushing injury of the knee or lower leg, with risk of compartment syndrome.

S88.d: Traumatic loss of the lower limb at the knee or lower leg level.

S89.n: Other and unspecified injuries of lower leg
S89.d: Other and unspecified injuries of the lower leg, including multiple injuries of the region.

S90.n: Superficial injury of ankle and foot
S90.d: Superficial injury of the ankle, foot and toes, such as contusion and abrasion.

S91.n: Open wound of ankle and foot
S91.d: Open wound of the ankle, foot or toes, often from a puncturing object, with risk of infection.

S92.d: Fracture of the calcaneus, talus, metatarsals or phalanges of the foot, excluding the ankle.

S93.n: Dislocation, sprain and strain of joints and ligaments at ankle and foot level
S93.d: Dislocation or ligament injury of the ankle and foot, such as lateral ankle sprain.

S94.n: Injury of nerves at ankle and foot level
S94.d: Traumatic injury of the plantar, deep fibular or cutaneous nerves at ankle and foot level.

S95.n: Injury of blood vessels at ankle and foot level
S95.d: Traumatic injury of the dorsalis pedis or plantar arteries or veins of the ankle and foot.

S96.n: Injury of muscle and tendon at ankle and foot level
S96.d: Injury of muscles and tendons at ankle and foot level, such as injury of the fibular (peroneal) and extensor tendons.

S97.n: Crushing injury of ankle and foot
S97.d: Crushing injury of the ankle, foot or toes.

S98.n: Traumatic amputation of ankle and foot
S98.d: Traumatic loss of the foot, part of it or toes, at or below the ankle.

S99.n: Other and unspecified injuries of ankle and foot
S99.d: Other and unspecified injuries of the ankle and foot, including multiple injuries of the region.

T00.n: Superficial injuries involving multiple body regions
T00.d: Simultaneous superficial injuries in more than one body region, such as multiple contusions and abrasions.

T01.n: Open wounds involving multiple body regions
T01.d: Simultaneous open wounds in more than one body region.

T02.d: Simultaneous fractures in more than one body region, usually from high-energy trauma.

T03.n: Dislocations, sprains and strains involving multiple body regions
T03.d: Simultaneous dislocations, sprains or strains in more than one body region.

T04.n: Crushing injuries involving multiple body regions
T04.d: Crushing injuries in more than one body region, with risk of rhabdomyolysis and kidney failure.

T05.n: Traumatic amputations involving multiple body regions
T05.d: Traumatic loss of limb segments in more than one body region.

T06.n: Other injuries involving multiple body regions, not elsewhere classified
T06.d: Other multiple injuries, such as simultaneous injuries of nerves, vessels or organs in different regions.

T07.d: Records multiple trauma without specification of the injuries or the regions involved.

T08.d: Vertebral fracture without specification of the spinal level involved.

T09.n: Other injuries of spine and trunk, level unspecified
T09.d: Other injuries of the spine and trunk without specification of level, such as unspecified spinal cord or ligament injury.

T10.n: Fracture of upper limb, level unspecified
T10.d: Fracture of the upper limb without specification of the bone or level.

T11.n: Other injuries of upper limb, level unspecified
T11.d: Other injuries of the upper limb without specification of level, such as wounds, dislocations or nerve injuries.

T12.n: Fracture of lower limb, level unspecified
T12.d: Fracture of the lower limb without specification of the bone or level.

T13.n: Other injuries of lower limb, level unspecified
T13.d: Other injuries of the lower limb without specification of level, such as wounds, dislocations or nerve injuries.

T14.d: Records trauma when the body region is not specified, useful when the available information is insufficient.

T15.d: Presence of a foreign body in the cornea, conjunctiva or conjunctival sac.

T16.d: Presence of a foreign body in the external auditory canal, common in children.

T17.d: Presence of a foreign body in the airways, from the nose to the bronchi, due to inhalation or aspiration.
s: Recurrent pneumonia at the same site

T18.d: Presence of an ingested foreign body in the mouth, esophagus, stomach, intestine or anus.

T19.d: Presence of a foreign body in the urethra, bladder, vagina or uterus.
