T20.n: Burn and corrosion of head and neck
T20.d: Thermal or chemical injury of the skin of the head and neck, with risk of airway involvement.

T21.d: Thermal or chemical injury of the trunk, including the chest, abdomen, back, perineum and genitalia.

T22.n: Burn and corrosion of shoulder and upper limb, except wrist and hand
T22.d: Thermal or chemical injury of the shoulder and upper limb, excluding the wrist and hand.

T23.n: Burn and corrosion of wrist and hand
T23.d: Thermal or chemical injury of the skin and tissues of the wrist and hand, graded by depth, with functional risk from scar contracture.
s: Whitish or brownish eschar in deep lesions

T24.n: Burn and corrosion of hip and lower limb, except ankle and foot
T24.d: Injury from heat, electricity, radiation or a chemical agent to the skin of the hip, thigh, knee or lower leg, classified by depth.
s: Risk of compartment syndrome in circumferential burns

T25.n: Burn and corrosion of ankle and foot
T25.d: Thermal or chemical injury of the skin of the ankle and foot, with risk of infection and of contracture that impairs gait.

T26.n: Burn and corrosion confined to eye and adnexa
T26.d: Thermal or chemical injury of the eyelid, conjunctiva or cornea; alkalis penetrate deeper and cause more severe eye damage than acids.

T27.n: Burn and corrosion of respiratory tract
T27.d: Thermal injury of the airway or injury from inhalation of smoke and chemicals, with laryngeal edema and damage to the bronchial and alveolar mucosa.
s: Facial burn and singed nasal hairs

T28.n: Burn and corrosion of other internal organs
T28.d: Thermal or chemical injury of internal organs, typically of the esophagus and stomach after ingestion of caustics or very hot liquids.

T29.n: Burns and corrosions of multiple body regions
T29.d: Burns or corrosions affecting several body regions, with severity defined by extent and depth.

T30.n: Burn and corrosion, body region unspecified
T30.d: Burn or corrosion recorded without indication of the body region, used when the location was not documented.

T31.n: Burns classified according to extent of body surface involved
T31.d: Supplementary code that records the percentage of body surface area burned, the basis for estimating severity and fluid replacement.

T32.n: Corrosions classified according to extent of body surface involved
T32.d: Supplementary code that records the percentage of body surface area affected by a chemical agent, used to estimate severity.

T33.d: Cold injury limited to the skin, with partial freezing of the epidermis and no permanent tissue loss.

T34.d: Deep freezing of tissues with vascular and cellular injury that progresses to necrosis and possible loss of parts.

T35.n: Frostbite involving multiple body regions and unspecified frostbite
T35.d: Cold injury in several body regions or with no region specified, usually after prolonged exposure to cold.
s: Pallor and coldness of the extremities

T36.d: Poisoning from overdose or misuse of systemic antibiotics, with toxicity depending on the drug class.

T37.n: Poisoning by other systemic anti-infectives and antiparasitics
T37.d: Poisoning by non-antibiotic antimicrobials, such as antimalarials, antituberculosis drugs, antifungals, antivirals and anthelmintics.

T38.n: Poisoning by hormones and their synthetic substitutes and antagonists, not elsewhere classified
T38.d: Poisoning by hormones and their antagonists, such as insulin, oral antidiabetics, levothyroxine, corticosteroids and estrogens.
s: Tachycardia and tremor with thyroid hormone

T39.n: Poisoning by nonopioid analgesics, antipyretics and antirheumatics
T39.d: Poisoning by non-opioid analgesics, especially paracetamol, salicylates and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.
s: Tinnitus, hyperventilation and acidosis with salicylates

T40.d: Poisoning by opioids, cocaine, cannabis and hallucinogens, with depressant or stimulant effects depending on the drug.
s: Miosis, bradypnea and drowsiness with opioids
Tachycardia, hypertension and agitation with cocaine
Response to naloxone in opioid poisoning

T41.n: Poisoning by anaesthetics and therapeutic gases
T41.d: Poisoning by general and local anesthetics or therapeutic gases, with neurological depression or cardiac toxicity.
s: Seizures and arrhythmias with local anesthetics

T42.n: Poisoning by antiepileptic, sedative-hypnotic and antiparkinsonism drugs
T42.d: Poisoning by anticonvulsants, benzodiazepines, barbiturates and antiparkinsonian drugs, with predominant nervous system depression.

T43.n: Poisoning by psychotropic drugs, not elsewhere classified
T43.d: Poisoning by antidepressants, antipsychotics and psychostimulants, with anticholinergic, serotonergic or cardiotoxic effects.
s: Wide QRS and arrhythmias with tricyclics

T44.n: Poisoning by drugs primarily affecting the autonomic nervous system
T44.d: Poisoning by drugs acting on the autonomic nervous system, such as anticholinesterases, anticholinergics, and adrenergic agonists and blockers.

T45.n: Poisoning by primarily systemic and haematological agents, not elsewhere classified
T45.d: Poisoning by antiallergics, antiemetics, vitamins, anticoagulants, thrombolytics, iron and antineoplastics, among others.

T46.n: Poisoning by agents primarily affecting the cardiovascular system
T46.d: Poisoning by cardiovascular drugs, such as digitalis glycosides, beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers and antihypertensives.

T47.n: Poisoning by agents primarily affecting the gastrointestinal system
T47.d: Poisoning by gastrointestinal drugs, such as antacids, laxatives, antidiarrheals and antiemetics.
s: Diarrhea and fluid-electrolyte disturbances with laxatives
Ileus and drowsiness with opioid antidiarrheals

T48.n: Poisoning by agents primarily acting on smooth and skeletal muscles and the respiratory system
T48.d: Poisoning by oxytocics, muscle relaxants, antiasthmatics and antitussives, with muscular, respiratory or cardiac effects.

T49.n: Poisoning by topical agents primarily affecting skin and mucous membrane and by ophthalmological, otorhinolaryngological and dental drugs
T49.d: Poisoning by topical skin, ophthalmic, otologic or dental drugs, usually from accidental ingestion or excessive absorption.
s: Neurological depression with imidazolines in children

T50.n: Poisoning by diuretics and other and unspecified drugs, medicaments and biological substances
T50.d: Poisoning by diuretics, fluid-electrolyte correcting agents, vaccines, contrast media and unspecified drugs.
s: Systemic reactions depending on the agent

T51.d: Acute poisoning by ethanol, methanol or other alcohols; methanol and ethylene glycol cause severe metabolic acidosis.
s: Depressed level of consciousness and ataxia
High anion gap acidosis in methanol poisoning

T52.d: Poisoning by organic solvents such as benzene, toluene and petroleum derivatives, inhaled or ingested.

T53.n: Toxic effect of halogen derivatives of aliphatic and aromatic hydrocarbons
T53.d: Poisoning by halogenated hydrocarbons, such as carbon tetrachloride and chloroform, with hepatic, renal and cardiac toxicity.

T54.d: Chemical injury from corrosive acids and alkalis, mainly by ingestion, with necrosis of the digestive mucosa.

T55.n: Toxic effect of soaps and detergents
T55.d: Poisoning by soaps and detergents, usually from accidental ingestion by children, with digestive irritation.
s: Risk of aspiration with concentrated pods

T56.d: Acute or chronic poisoning by metals such as lead, mercury, arsenic and cadmium, with neurological, renal and hematological damage.
s: Anemia with basophilic stippling in lead poisoning

T57.n: Toxic effect of other inorganic substances
T57.d: Poisoning by inorganic substances such as phosphorus, hydrogen cyanide and other nonmetallic compounds.

T58.d: Tissue hypoxia due to binding of carbon monoxide to hemoglobin, forming carboxyhemoglobin, usually in enclosed spaces with combustion.

T59.n: Toxic effect of other gases, fumes and vapours
T59.d: Poisoning by irritant or asphyxiant gases and vapors, such as chlorine, ammonia, hydrogen sulfide and smoke.

T60.d: Poisoning by pesticides, notably organophosphates and carbamates, which inhibit acetylcholinesterase.

T61.n: Toxic effect of noxious substances eaten as seafood
T61.d: Poisoning by toxins present in fish and seafood, such as ciguatera, scombroid and shellfish toxins.
s: Flushing and headache in scombroid poisoning
Reversal of temperature sensation in ciguatera
Weakness and paralysis in severe cases

T62.n: Toxic effect of other noxious substances eaten as food
T62.d: Poisoning from ingestion of poisonous mushrooms, plants or berries mistaken for food.

T63.n: Toxic effect of contact with venomous animals
T63.d: Envenomation by snakes, scorpions, spiders, bees, caterpillars or marine animals.
s: Ptosis and blurred vision in Crotalus envenomation
Sweating and vomiting in scorpion envenomation

T64.n: Toxic effect of aflatoxin and other mycotoxin food contaminants
T64.d: Toxic effect of mycotoxins from fungi that contaminate grains and foods; aflatoxin is hepatotoxic and carcinogenic.
s: Risk of hepatocellular carcinoma with chronic exposure

T65.n: Toxic effect of other and unspecified substances
T65.d: Toxic effect of substances not classified in other categories, such as cyanides, nicotine, paints and dyes, or of an unidentified agent.

T66.d: Unspecified acute effects of ionizing radiation, including acute radiation syndrome, depending on the absorbed dose.

T67.d: Conditions caused by environmental heat, such as heatstroke, heat exhaustion, heat cramps and heat syncope, due to failure of thermoregulation.

T68.d: Drop in core temperature below 35 °C due to cold exposure, with progressive depression of organ functions.
s: Arrhythmias and coma in severe cases

T69.d: Non-freezing cold injuries, such as immersion foot and chilblains, due to prolonged exposure to wet cold.

T70.n: Effects of air pressure and water pressure
T70.d: Injuries from changes in atmospheric or water pressure, such as barotrauma, decompression sickness and altitude sickness.
s: Ear pain and hearing loss in barotrauma

T71.d: Oxygen deprivation due to mechanical obstruction of breathing, chest compression or an oxygen-poor environment.

T73.d: Conditions caused by deprivation of food, water or shelter, or by excessive exertion and prolonged exposure.

T74.d: Physical, sexual or psychological injuries and neglect inflicted on children, older adults or partners, recognized by the pattern of injuries.

T75.d: Effects of external causes such as lightning, nonfatal drowning, vibration, motion sickness and electric shock.
s: Entry and exit burns in electric shock
Nausea and vomiting in motion sickness

T78.d: Adverse reactions not attributed to a specific agent, including food anaphylaxis, angioedema and unspecified allergy.

T79.n: Certain early complications of trauma, not elsewhere classified
T79.d: Early complications of trauma, such as fat embolism, traumatic shock, compartment syndrome and post-traumatic renal failure.
s: Hypoxemia and petechiae in fat embolism

T80.n: Complications following infusion, transfusion and therapeutic injection
T80.d: Complications of infusions, transfusions and injections, such as hemolytic reaction, air embolism, infection and serum reaction.
s: Low back pain and hemoglobinuria in hemolysis

T81.n: Complications of procedures, not elsewhere classified
T81.d: Complications of medical procedures, such as hemorrhage, shock, dehiscence, wound infection and retained foreign body.

T82.n: Complications of cardiac and vascular prosthetic devices, implants and grafts
T82.d: Mechanical, infectious or thrombotic complications of prosthetic valves, pacemakers, stents and vascular grafts.

T83.n: Complications of genitourinary prosthetic devices, implants and grafts
T83.d: Complications of urinary catheters, ureteral stents, penile prostheses and intrauterine devices.

T84.n: Complications of internal orthopaedic prosthetic devices, implants and grafts
T84.d: Complications of joint prostheses and osteosynthesis hardware, such as loosening, dislocation, implant fracture and infection.

T85.n: Complications of other internal prosthetic devices, implants and grafts
T85.d: Complications of internal devices such as ventricular shunts, breast implants, intraocular lenses and peritoneal dialysis catheters.

T86.n: Failure and rejection of transplanted organs and tissues
T86.d: Loss of graft function due to immunological rejection or other failure of a transplanted organ or tissue.
s: Worsening function of the grafted organ

T87.n: Complications peculiar to reattachment and amputation
T87.d: Complications of the amputation stump and of reattached segments, such as infection, necrosis, neuroma and phantom pain.

T88.n: Other complications of surgical and medical care, not elsewhere classified
T88.d: Complications of medical care not classified elsewhere, such as malignant hyperthermia, anesthetic shock and adverse reaction to a correctly administered drug.
s: Hyperthermia and rigidity in malignant hyperthermia
